### The monospaced font's ligatures are off (2026-10-27)

- Fira Code draws ligatures. A record's text changed on screen: the game id k3x9q showed as k3×9q, and "??" showed as
  one glyph. A player who copies or reads an id, a move or a record must see the characters that are there.
- The rule is one line in `packages/site/src/site.css`: `--font-mono--font-feature-settings: "liga" 0, "calt" 0` in
  the theme, next to `--font-mono`. Tailwind 4 gives the setting wherever it gives the font: the `font-mono` utility,
  and preflight's `code`, `kbd`, `samp` and `pre`. No other rule in either site takes `--font-mono`. So the setting
  covers every monospaced text of Hedge School and Drawing Board: the records, the move lists, the Notation page and
  the editor.
- Fira Code has all of its ligatures in the `calt` feature, and no `liga`. `"liga" 0` stays for a fallback font.
  Measured in headless Chromium on both sites' builds: with `"calt" 0` alone, k3x9q, `????.??.??`, `=>`, `!=`, `->`,
  `0x1F` and `www` draw the same pixels as with the rule. With `"liga" 0` alone, they draw their ligatures.
- Fira Code's ligatures keep the grid: a ligature of two characters takes two cells. Each of those texts measured 0.6
  em a character with the ligatures on and off. So the move list's columns, sized in `ch`, keep their width. The book
  table's edge (A10-D10, 7 `ch`) draws the same with the ligatures on and off.
- The test is in `apps/hedgeschool/tests/layout.spec.ts`. It checks the `font-feature-settings` of the `font-mono`
  utility, and of every element in Fira Code on the Notation page and on Hedge School's editor, whose position field
  is in Fira Code. It also checks the width of a probe text. The Drawing Board test runs when `DB_BASE_URL` gives its
  preview.

### A mark on each book move, in two forms (2026-10-27)

- **Each book move has a mark** (design 32, item 4; beads abscls-tpaj.17): an edge whose position and the position
  after it are both in the book. The mark takes the quality label's slot in the move list, whatever the label, from
  Great to Blunder. By turn, a turn has it when all its edges are book moves. It replaces the one mark at the last
  book move of each stretch, "Last move in the book". Nothing said what that mark meant without a pointer, and the
  moves before it carried nothing, so it did not show how far the game followed the book.
- **No special rule for poor moves.** A book icon with the quality label in its place on a Great, Inaccuracy, Mistake
  or Blunder book move was not chosen: a book move that the review calls an Inaccuracy or worse would then never show
  as a book move. Every book move has the mark, and the mark shows the quality label.
- **Two forms, a display setting** ("Book moves", beside "Quality labels"): the quality label on the book's brown
  (the default), or an open book in the quality label's colour. As a badge: the quality mark in white on a brown
  disc, or the book in white on the quality label's disc. As a quality mark alone: the quality mark in the brown, or
  the book in the quality label's colour. The default follows Chess.com, whose Book mark is a brown disc. Both forms
  depart from Chess.com, whose "Book" takes the place of the move's quality label: a book move can still be a poor
  one.
- **The previews** were drawn into the review of `book-left-review.json`, light and dark, by edge and by turn. Each
  preview gave one form:
  - The book in the quality label's colour. It is now the second form.
  - The quality label's badge with a small book tab. At this size, the tab reads as a dot.
  - One book icon on the brown. It hides the move's quality.
  - The quality mark in white on the brown. It is now the default.
  - The quality mark in its own colour on the brown. The quality labels' colours have 1.04:1 (Best) to 1.47:1
    (Inaccuracy) against the brown, so these marks almost disappear.
- **The brown,** `--book` in `packages/review/src/review.css`, at least 3:1 against the panel and panel-2:

  | Theme | Colour | Against the panel | Against panel-2 | White on it |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Light | #a4835e | 3.51:1 | 3.03:1 | 3.51:1 |
  | Dark | #a88865 (Chess.com's) | 4.48:1 | 3.91:1 | 3.29:1 |

  Chess.com's #a88865 has 2.84:1 against the light panel-2 (#f0eeea), under the floor. #a4835e keeps its hue and
  saturation in HSL, and is the lightest such colour at 3:1 against panel-2. White on a label's badge is 2.32:1 on
  Good, 2.24:1 on Inaccuracy and 2.78:1 on Excellent, so white on the brown reads as well or better.
- **The title and accessible name** are the move's own tooltip, with "Book move" before it and the position symbol
  after the move at its end (the book's minimaxed value of that position, in the symbol's words): "Book move · Best:
  +0.6% · +2.0 · Lead: Blue +14.9 · Equal position after it". By turn, the turn's tooltip and the position after the
  turn. A title with the quality label and the position alone ("Book move: Good. Blue is slightly better after it.")
  was not chosen: the mark is inside the move's button, so its title covers the button's, and that title hid the
  move's numbers. The mark's title and the move's come from one value, so they cannot drift apart.
- **The mark has no click or preview of its own.** The old mark, "Last move in the book", went to the position before
  its move and showed the book there, and this change first kept that click. By edge, pointing at the mark still
  previewed the position after the move, because the mark is inside the move's button. So a first build previewed the
  position before the move on the mark alone. The click and that preview were confusing, and unlike every other
  quality label in the move list. This change removes both. The mark behaves as a quality label does in the same
  slot. By edge, pointing at it previews the position after the move, and a click goes there, as on the rest of the
  move's button. By turn, the first version of this change left the slot in the turn's cell, which had no preview and
  no click. The book's table stays reachable at any position (the Book view, the key o).
- **By edge and by turn, a row's parts behave the same** (the owner's words on that version, 2026-10-30: "by edge and
  by turn shouldn't have this behavior difference"). "Review by" changes how the move list groups the moves, not how
  its parts behave. By edge, the move's button holds the label slot, the ◆ and the loss figure. By turn, these three
  are now one button, the turn's whole judgement cell. Its label slot holds a quality label or the book mark.
  Pointing anywhere in the cell previews the position after the turn (after its last edge), with the status line of a
  move. A click goes there. "Preview played moves" off turns the preview off. A first build made the label slot alone
  a button, and the ◆ and the loss figure still did nothing by turn. The quality labels had the difference before
  this change: by turn, pointing at one and clicking it did nothing. By edge, nothing changes. The cell keeps its
  widths. Design 06 states the rule. The review of the change found one more difference. By edge, a right-click on a
  quality label opens its move's menu, with "Generate image". By turn, a right-click on the cell opened the menu with
  each action off. The cell now opens the menu of the turn's last edge. One function gives the move's button and the
  cell their click, preview and menu, so the two cannot drift apart again. The label slot is one snippet too: by edge
  and by turn, a quality label's word names it for assistive technology (by edge it had no name), and its label
  stands at the slot's left (the cell's button had centred it).
- **The setting "Book moves" shows only where the book loaded.** It offered itself wherever the review had a book
  place, also when the book did not load, and then it changed nothing.
- **No mark** on the live site, where the book does not load, on a set-up board and on the Analysis board, as with the
  mark before. A book move with no quality label yet, or of the player that "Review for" leaves out, has no mark. A
  move that comes back to the book from a position outside it is not a book move: in `book-never-review.json`, G14-H11
  had the old mark and has none now.

### The book's table follows Review by: whole turns at a turn's start (2026-10-27)

- **What:** the book's table follows the display setting "Review by", as the review's labels do (design 32, item 3).
  By turn, the default, a turn's start lists whole turns: each book move, then each book move of the position that it
  reaches. A row names both edges. Its win chance is the one after the second edge, and its quality label comes from
  the turn's loss against the best turn, by design 10's rule for a turn. By edge, and in a turn's middle, the rows
  stay single edges. The book holds the position after each edge, with its minimaxed values, so the switch needs no
  new search: the page loads the parts that hold the positions after the turn start's book moves. A turn's start
  where no book move has a book move after it lists single edges too. The test book has no such start.
- **One row a position:** two orders of the same two edges reach the same position, so they are one row, with the
  order whose first edge the book prefers. The first build gave each order a row: at turn 3 of the test game
  book-left-review.json, D9-G10 D10-G9 (Best) and D10-G9 D9-G10 (Excellent) were two rows, both 58.1%. In the test
  book, 31 of the 284 whole turns at turn starts are a second order of another, at 24 of the 78 turn starts. No merge
  drops a trap's order for an order that is not a trap.
- **The test book's counts** (`rows.test.ts`), with one row a position: 78 turn starts after turn 1 have book moves.
  They give a median of 1 whole turn and at most 33 (turn 3 after Blue's D10-G9 and Red's N11-Q10 O11-Q10: 5 fine
  turns, 20 others and 8 traps), and 6 of them give more than 8. With a row for each order, the counts were at most
  34 and 8 above 8. Beads abscls-tpaj.18 had counted 79 turn starts and 9 above 8. In every turn start, the value
  after a book move equals the best of its position's book moves and its best move outside the book. So the best
  turn's win chance is the position's best: the first book move's, or the best move outside the book's.
- **The best 8:** the fine and the other turns, by the win chance for the side to move. The rest come after a button
  ("Show 11 more turns" for 19), before the traps. The traps and the best turn outside the book always show: in the
  start with 33 turns, the first 8 rows of the table would have put the 8 traps under the button. So 5 of the 6
  starts above 8 have the button. The board numbers only the rows that show.
- **The best turn outside the book:** the best for the side to move of two kinds of turn. The first kind is the
  position's best first edge outside the book, whose second edge the book does not hold. The second kind is a book
  move, then the best second edge outside the book after it. In the test book, the first kind is the best at 48 turn
  starts, and the second at 30.
- **A trap's turn:** a second edge's trap keeps its refutation (the enemy's turn, 2 edges for all 25 of the test
  book's). A first edge's trap (13 at turn starts) gives each of its turns: after the second edge that its refutation
  starts with, the rest of the refutation, and after another, none. In the test book, a first edge's trap has 1 to 5
  book moves after it.
- **The Report's opening row:** by turn it names the turn that left the book, with the review's quality label of the
  turn, and goes to the turn's start. "Blue, D9-G11 D10-G9, Blunder" in the test game book-left-review.json, where
  by edge it says "D9-G11" and the edge's quality label. Its "Before that" names a whole book turn too. The
  candidates are the game's turns before the departure whose edges are all book moves and none a trap. The row names
  the one worse than Good with the largest loss, with the quality label that the table gives the turn. In
  book-left-review.json: "Before that, at turn 2, Red played N11-Q10 O11-Q10, a book turn and an Inaccuracy." (a
  loss of 0.077), where by edge it names O11-Q10. A game whose weak turn reached the end: "The last book turn, D9-G10
  G10-J13, is a Mistake." (0.105), where G10-J13 alone is an Inaccuracy. The trap rows do not change. The row names
  the worst whole book turn, not always the last one, as by edge it names the worst book move. In
  book-left-review.json the worst is also the last.
- **The width:** by turn, a row's two edges take 154 pixels, and the table needs 313 pixels with its heads on one
  line. A window 360 pixels wide gives the table's box 264 pixels with its scroll bars (the layout test), and 294
  in a phone's emulation, whose scroll bars take no room (`tests/book-review.spec.ts`). With the head "Line ends" on
  two lines alone, the table still needed 282 pixels. The first build let the heads "Blue wins" and "Line ends" take
  two lines and halved the cells' padding in a box under 320 pixels wide: the head row was then 49 pixels high, where
  by edge it is 29. Now a turn's edges wrap: where the column has no room for both, the second edge and the badge go
  under the first. The table then needs no more width than by edge, every head stays on one line, and every row wraps
  at the same width, so the badges stay at one place (`npm run test:layout`, `tests/book-review.spec.ts`). The rows
  take a line more there, and the words and the font keep their size. In a window 360 pixels wide with scroll bars,
  by turn as by edge, the head row is 29 pixels high, and the heads are 28, 96, 72 ("Blue wins" and "Red wins") and
  68 pixels wide, in a table of 264 pixels in its box of 264. A turn's row there is 49 pixels high, where an edge's
  row is 29 (turn 2 of book-left-review.json). At 1,366 pixels a turn's row is one line.
- **The move list by edge** hides 56 pixels sideways from 360 to 410 pixels wide (320 pixels of rows in 264), with
  or without the book, and fits by turn. The layout test swept the review by turn only, so it never met this
  (beads abscls-8n02). The book's sweep by edge left out this one fault until the fix, and checked the rest.
- **The fix of the move list by edge:** each move takes 139 pixels by edge, so a row of two needs 320. Each row now
  wraps: where a turn's two moves do not fit side by side, the second move goes under the first, at its own width, so
  that its quality label and its loss stay next to its notation. By edge the rows wrap at 360, 385 and 410 pixels
  wide (move lists of 264, 289 and 314 pixels) and hide nothing. From 420 pixels, a turn is one line again, also at
  1,260 to 1,300 pixels, where the move list has its least width of 325 pixels (design 06). By turn nothing changed.
  The first build wrapped below a fixed width of 21.5 rem. That wrapped every turn of Practice's move list, whose
  moves have no labels and need about 180 pixels, and every row by edge at 1,260 to 1,300 pixels. A wrapping row wraps
  only where the two moves do not fit, for every move list and every game's moves. The book's sweep by edge now runs
  in full (`npm run test:layout`: 53 passed, 7 skipped).

### The Opening row gives the review's label of the earlier book move (2026-10-27)

Beads abscls-tpaj.21. Replaced on 2026-10-30: the review takes a book position's values from the book, so the
review's label of a book move is the book's ("A book move takes the book's label and loss", below).

- **What:** the Report's Opening row names the worst earlier book move by the review's quality labels, not the book's.
  It names a move that the review labels worse than Good: the worst label first (Inaccuracy, then Mistake, then
  Blunder), and between equal labels the larger loss by the review's values. By turn it names the worst whole book
  turn, by the review's label of the turn. When no earlier book move has such a label, the row says nothing of one. A
  trap keeps its own row. A move that the review has not labeled yet, or has no label for (the player that "Review
  for" leaves out), is not named. The departure's part of the row is as before: it already had the review's label.
- **Why:** one page gave one move two labels. In book-left-review.json, the row said "Before that, at turn 2, Red
  played O11-Q10, a book move and an Inaccuracy." (by turn: "N11-Q10 O11-Q10, a book turn and an Inaccuracy"), which
  is the label of the book's search (`gameOpening`'s `weak` and `weakTurn`). The move list and the move's book mark
  gave the review's label, Good (a loss of 4.2% by edge, 3.3% by turn). Design 32 says that one engine and one depth
  rule a game's labels in the review, on book moves too. The two labels differ by design in the book's table, which
  shows the book's values. They must not differ in the Report, which is part of the review. Now the row for that game
  says "The game left the book at turn 3: Blue, D9-G11, Blunder." and nothing of O11-Q10.
- **How:** `openingRow` takes a function from an edge's index to the review's label and loss (by turn, of the turn
  that starts there), which `ReviewView.svelte` builds from the labels that it shows (`shownJudgment`). The book code
  chooses the move from them (`worstBookPlay` in `game.ts`). `GameOpening` keeps the book moves before the departure
  (`earlier` and `earlierTurns`) in place of the book's own choice (`weak` and `weakTurn`), and the sentences take
  the label as an argument. The book's loss and label of a played move no longer reach the row.

### A book move takes the book's label and loss: the review takes a book position's values from the book (2026-10-30)

Beads abscls-tpaj.21 and abscls-tpaj.22. It replaces the decision of 2026-10-27 ("The Opening row gives the review's
label of the earlier book move", above), and the choice of 2026-10-24 that the review keeps its own labels in the book.

- **What:** where the book's label of a book move and the review's differ, the book's label stands. A book move takes
  the book's quality label and loss everywhere on the page: the move list, its book mark, the Report's Opening row,
  the charts and the counts. The way to it: at each position of the game that the book holds, the review takes the
  book's values in place of searching the position (design 32, "A book position's values"). The review's own rules
  (design 10) then give the book's labels, and the review does not search the opening.
- **Why:** the book's searches are the deeper (design 32, item 5): an opening book is made with the most search. A
  review that keeps its own labels gave one move two labels on one page, the table's and the move list's.
- **How:** `bookAnalysis` and `bookResults` (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/book/results.ts`) make a search's result from
  a book position: its value, its candidates (the book moves and the best move outside the book, the best first), its
  complexity and its area map, with `book` set. `GameAnalysis.useBook` takes them by the game's index, and `giveBook`
  (`reviewBook.ts`) gives them once the book's parts load: on the review page, on a review snapshot and in the
  annotated record from the store. `data()` gives the book's values in `analysis` and the engine's own results in
  `searched`, which the analysis column shows. The stages, the variations' evaluations and the map stage search no
  book position. The model judges the book's values as deep enough at any depth and gives no Great from or into a book
  position. A label rounds its loss to 6 decimals (`classify`), as the book's rule does.
- **Settled:** the move that leaves the book compares the book's value with a search, and is never Great. A book that
  loads late gives its values as they come, and the stages skip the positions that still wait. A book that does not
  load gives none, and the review searches every position. A review stored before keeps its results in the store,
  and its labels take the book's values. The Analysis board and a set-up board take no book values. One review now
  mixes two networks, the book's and the review's.
- **Measured:** a unit test reads every book move of the test book through the review's model with the book's values:
  the label and the loss are the table's for 434 edges and 284 whole turns (both orders of a turn), and for each edge
  of those turns by edge. Without the rounding, one edge went to the next band. In book-left-review.json, O11-Q10 is
  an Inaccuracy, −7.7% and −17.9 points, by edge, and N11-Q10 O11-Q10 the same by turn. The Opening row says "The
  game left the book at turn 3: Blue, D9-G11, Blunder. Before that, at turn 2, Red played O11-Q10, a book move and an
  Inaccuracy." (by turn: "Blue, D9-G11 D10-G9, Blunder. Before that, at turn 2, Red played N11-Q10 O11-Q10, a book
  turn and an Inaccuracy."). A10-D9 is Best at 0.0%, where the review's search gave it +0.6%.
- **The best turn in the other order, by edge:** design 10 makes both edges of the engine's best turn in the other
  order Best. From the book's values, that rule gave the turn's first edge Best where the table by edge gives it its
  own label: at `A10-D10,D10-G9* Q10-T10 r2 0/0 1`, Red's O11-Q10 N11-Q10 gave O11-Q10 Best, and the table gives it
  Excellent (a loss of 0). The rule does not apply to an edge between two positions with the book's values (`review`
  in `model.ts`). It still applies to an edge that leaves the book or comes into it.
- **A Great after the book:** the review's labels read the book's value at the position before the other player's last
  turn, but the Greats' confirmations read the engine's result there, which the stages did not search. So no
  confirmation was asked for, and the move could not be Great. Both now read the book's value (`earlierAt`).
- **A review snapshot** of a review made with the book did not open, because its check of the store asked for a
  result at the book's positions, which the review did not search (beads abscls-tpaj.22). The check now leaves out
  the positions that the book holds, once the rules give the positions and the book its values. The removal of
  earlier results reads no book: for a mark that names its search, it keeps that search's results where they hold
  any position of the game's line (`searchHolding`'s `holds`). So it can keep the results of a review snapshot that
  does not open, until the game is reviewed again. A mark that names no search is older than the book: its review
  snapshot and the removal ask for every position, as before.

### Drawing Board's import page opens the review and the Analysis board (2026-11-01)

abscls-8tl1.18. Design 33, "How a game comes in from strategyjam.org", items 5 and 6, gives the result. The choices
that the designs left open:

- **The engine checks the record before the page offers the choice,** not after a click. A record that the engine
  refuses then shows no button that would fail. The check starts a rules worker of its own, and ends it after
  (`checkRecord` in `recordCheck.ts`, as Hedge School's `checkMoves` starts one): the rules alone need no network.
  Without the engine's files, the page refuses the record, since no page can check it. No test measures the wait
  alone: in the browser tests (headless Chromium, 2 workers, the engine on the CPU), a test of an out-of-date tool,
  from the page's load to the choice, took 7.7 to 8.2 s, and the refused record's test 8.1 to 9.9 s. The page shows
  the game while the engine checks it.
- **The page sends the record by each page's own address** (`/review#record=`, `/analysis#record=…&at=`), which
  already took a record and checked it. Hedge School's import keeps the game itself and opens `/review#game=`, since
  its review has a list of games. Drawing Board's review keeps one game, under the key that the review writes. So the
  engine checks the record twice, once on each page: the review's check is part of its start, and costs nothing more.
- **The choice's frame moved to `packages/import`** (`ToolChoice.svelte`): the notice's place, the game's line, and
  the two ways, each a button with what it does. Each site gives its own words. While the engine checks the record,
  a line says so in the ways' place (`pending`), so the game's lines do not move when the ways come. Hedge School's
  import page gives the same markup as before, and its tests (`tool-choice.spec.ts`, the layout test's choice) are
  unchanged.
- **The Analysis board asks before a record replaces the analysis kept here,** as Hedge School's board does
  ("Replace your analysis?"), when that analysis has moves. The question moved to `packages/review`
  (`ReplaceAnalysis.svelte`): Hedge School's board gives the same markup and texts, and its test
  (`tool-choice.spec.ts`) is unchanged. Drawing Board's board asks once the engine accepts the record, so a refused
  record asks nothing. The choice's card no longer says that the game replaces the board's moves.
- **The record stays on the page, under "The record", closed.** It helps the test of the tools on strategyjam.org
  (abscls-8tl1.12), and it no longer takes the page's room.
- **No `via` in the board's address:** Drawing Board counts no import, so `analysisAddress` takes a source or null,
  and names none for null. Each caller states its source, so a Hedge School call cannot leave it out by mistake.
- **Drawing Board's accent is Hedge School's lavender** (`#6f5aa8` light, `#b8a6e8` dark), in place of the neutral
  slate of "Drawing Board's shell" (2026-10-25: `#4f5b69`, `#b4bcc7`), until Drawing Board's own colour comes with its
  logo. The slate read as a grey, and the site needs a colour. On the tokens that the sites share, the lavender has
  Hedge School's contrast: 5.2:1 as text on the page and 5.7:1 under white text, light, and 5.9:1 as text on panel-2
  and 8.2:1 under near-black text, dark.

### A book move played from the table takes the book's label: a variation's book positions (2026-11-02)

abscls-8981, left by the review of abscls-tpaj.21 ("A book move takes the book's label and loss", above).

- **What:** a book move that the player plays from the book's table becomes a variation of the game (design 07).
  "Evaluate quality" judged it by the book's value before it, where that position is the game's, and by an engine
  search after it. Its label could then differ from the table's row for the same move. Now each position of a
  variation that the book holds takes the book's values, as the game's positions do (design 32, "A book position's
  values"), and the evaluation does not search it. A position outside the book is searched, as before.
- **What the book's values replace:** `GameAnalysis.judge` marks the turn's variation moves, and `judgeSearches` queues
  a search of the positions before and after each, to the label budget, at the evaluation's priority. Their results go
  to the variation's nodes (`branches`, each node's `analysis`), and the view judges the move from them (`branchLabel`
  and `branchTurnAt` in `ReviewView.svelte`). Before the change, only the game's positions took the book's values
  (`bookAt` read `bookResults` by the game's index). Now `bookAt` reads a variation's position too. The view's
  `analysisAt` reads `GameAnalysis.valuesAt`: the book's values where the book holds the position, else the node's own
  search. The Greats' checks read `bookAt` already, so no move from or into a variation's book position is Great, as on
  the game's line.
- **How:** `giveBook` gives `useBook` a lookup by position (`bookValues` in `results.ts`), beside the game's values.
  The analysis asks it once for each variation position, when the tree adds the position or when the book comes. The
  evaluation waits for the answers of its positions, then searches the positions with no book values. A search that
  still waits for an engine when the book's values come is dropped (`wanted`).
- **Settled:** a book that loads after the evaluation started gives its values as they come, and the waiting searches
  of its positions are dropped. A search that ran before keeps its result for the analysis column. A book that does
  not load, or a lookup that fails, gives no values, and the evaluation searches the variation's positions, as before.
  The book holds positions, not lines: a variation that reaches a book position by another move order takes its
  values. The Analysis board and a set-up board take no book, so their variations are searched as before. The area
  map of a variation's book position is the book's too, as on the game's line (`mapAt` reads `bookAt`).
- **Measured:** unit tests. In the analysis package, with a book that holds two positions, "Evaluate quality" on a
  variation move between them searches nothing, and the move after it searches only the position outside the book. In
  the site, the test book judges K12-N11 after A10-D9 N11-Q10, a variation of book-left-review.json. By edge, the move
  gets the table's label, Inaccuracy, and its loss of 8.5%. By turn, N11-Q10 K12-N11 gets the label and the loss of
  the table's row. A browser test plays K12-N11 from the table with the engine off, by edge and by turn: "Evaluate
  quality" shows Inaccuracy in the move list and in the move's tooltip. Before the change the move list kept "…"
  there, by the code: the position after the move waited for a search that the engine, off, does not start. The test
  did not run on the code before the change.
- **The review's check by edge and by turn** (design 06, item 8): in headless Chromium, the move has the same
  tooltip and the same badge in both. Pointing at the move previews the position after it, and a click goes there.
  The badge after a variation's move is not part of its button in either unit: pointing at it and clicking it do
  nothing, as on any variation move that was evaluated.

### A move that the player asked to evaluate says "Evaluating…" only while a search can run (2026-11-02)

- **The fault:** a variation move that the player marked with "Evaluate quality" showed "Evaluating…" and a pulsing
  "…" whenever it had no label (`judged` and no label). It did so also with the engine off, when nothing evaluates it.
- **The rule** (design 07, item 11): the text and the pulse show while a search for the move can run or runs. A
  search can run while the engine is on, with its network loaded or still loading, and with no engine error. The
  engine's switch is its pause: the session sets `GameAnalysis.paused` from the switch. No search can run with the
  engine off, after an engine error (`GameAnalysis.error`), or in a review snapshot (design 20). The rule and the
  texts are in `searchWait.ts`. `ReviewView.svelte` gives it the analysis's own fields and reads it once
  (`whyNoSearch`).
- **Where none can,** the move says "Not analyzed yet", as the game's moves say it, and then why and what to do:
  "Not analyzed yet. The engine is off. To evaluate this move, set the engine switch to on.", "Not analyzed yet. The
  engine has an error." and "Not analyzed yet. A review snapshot does no searches." The pulsing "…" does not show.
  The words "engine is off" are the site's (the Threat line, the review bar: "Engine off. The review is paused.").
  The step is "set the engine switch to on", Simplified Technical English's form for a switch, not "turn it on": the
  standard forbids phrasal verbs.
- **Edge and turn, review and board:** one rule gives the variation move's tooltip, by edge and by turn, and the
  pulse after the move. It also gives the tooltips of the Analysis board's main-line moves that the player evaluated
  (`board.judged`: the edge's tooltip, the turn cell's). These get no "…": the game's moves have none. Before, they
  said "Not analyzed yet" also while their search ran. They now say "Evaluating…" then.
- **"Review for":** a player that the setting leaves out shows no labels, and now no wait either. Before, by edge, a
  judged variation move of that player kept the wait for good, because its label was hidden. It showed "Evaluating…"
  and the pulse with the engine on, and the engine-off text with the engine off. By turn, the wait ended with the
  judgement.
- **A move that would be Great** waits for its extra searches only while the engine is on and its network is loaded
  (`awaitsGreat`). Before that, or with the engine off, it shows the label that the searches done give (Best), not
  "Not analyzed yet".
- **An engine error** (`GameAnalysis.error`) stays with the analysis, and the other searches go on. The analysis does
  not keep the search that failed. So after an error, a move says "The engine has an error." also while its own
  search runs. Its label then comes as usual.
- **Not changed:** a game move in a review, which has no label yet because the review is under way, keeps its text.
  abscls-8981 covers a position that the book holds.
- **Tests:** `searchWait.test.ts` tests the rule in each state, "Evaluating…" included. `tests/search-wait.spec.ts`
  opens the Analysis board with the engine off, by edge and by turn. On a variation and on the main line, it checks
  the text and that nothing pulses. It also opens a review with "Review for" Blue, by edge and by turn: Red's
  evaluated moves say nothing. The browser tests keep the engine off, so "Evaluating…" has the unit test alone.

### A variation's label and ◆ act as its move, and its book move shows the book mark (2026-11-03)

abscls-exfe and abscls-gapn, built together, because both change what follows a variation's move in the move list.

- **What (abscls-exfe):** a variation move's quality label, its pulsing "…" and its ◆ stood after the move's button.
  Pointing at them and clicking them did nothing, unlike the game's moves (design 06, item 8). Now, by edge, they are
  inside the move's button, in each form of the variations (text, pills and dots). By turn, they are the turn's own
  button after the move that ends the turn ("The design by turn", below). Pointing at any of them previews the
  move's line, a click goes there, and a right-click opens the move's menu. Assistive technology reads the label's
  word, as on the game's line (`labelSlot`).
- **The turn's judgement cell** takes its last edge's state (`moveState`): the "here" outline when the board is after
  the turn, and the picked outline when the fork keys pick that edge. Before, it had the pointer's outline only. Now the
  pointer on it lights the turn's group instead ("The design by turn", below). The cell is no `.mv`, so `keepInView` and
  the tests still find one place on screen.
- **What (abscls-gapn):** a variation's book move showed its quality label, not the book mark that the game's book
  moves show (design 32, item 4). Now it shows the same mark, by the same rule, with the same settings and tooltip.
  The mark comes with the label, so only after "Evaluate quality", and "Review for" hides it with the label. By turn,
  a variation's turn shows the mark when all its edges are book moves. An edge of the game's line in that turn counts
  by the game's own mark (`bookMoves`). The mark shows only in a review whose book loaded, as the game's marks do. The
  Analysis board has none.
- **The data path:** the view asks the site's book about the two positions of one move, with the function that gives
  the game's marks (`BookParts.opening`, through `bookAfterAt` in `ReviewView.svelte`). This adds one function and no
  interface: the rule and the words of the position symbol are the game's. Other paths need more parts. The analysis
  (`GameAnalysis.branchBook`, abscls-8981) knows which variation positions the book holds, but not whether the book
  lists the move or the symbol after it, so it would need new fields and a new lookup. A new method on the book's
  interface would repeat `opening`'s rule. Each lookup can load a part of the book, so the move list asks only for a
  move that shows a label.
- **The round forms:** in pills and dots, by edge, the button grows into a capsule round the shape and its marks, and
  the "here" outline goes round all of them. By turn, the move's button stays round. Each part is as tall as its glyph
  (`leading-none`), so a label keeps the row's height.
- **Measured** in headless Chromium at 1366 × 900, on K12-N11 before and after "Evaluate quality", by edge and by turn
  alike, in the first build (the label in the move's button by turn too). Text: the button grows from 62.3 to 80.6 px
  wide, its height stays 21 px and its row 25 px. Pills: from 17 × 17.4 to 33.3 × 17.4 px, and the row stays 21.4 px.
  Dots: from 13.4 × 13.4 to 29.8 × 16.6 px, and the row stays 21.1 px. Before each part fitted its glyph, the label's
  line made the pills and dots buttons 19.2 px high and their rows 23.2 px. By turn, the cell of turn 2 is "here" after
  the turn, and the page has one `.mv.here`.
- **Tests:** `tests/book-review.spec.ts`, with the engine off, by edge and by turn. K12-N11, played from the book's
  table at turn 2 of book-left-review.json and evaluated, shows the book mark with its name, title and colour, in
  each form of the variations. Pointing at the mark previews the line, a click goes there, and a right-click opens
  the move's menu. A review file with two variations and their stored results (made in the test from
  book-left-review.json) gives a move outside the book, with its plain label, and a move after a hard position, with
  the ◆. Their label and ◆ act as the move. By turn, the judgement cell is "here" after its turn, not in the turn's
  middle, and picked with its last edge.
- **The design by turn,** decided on pages that drew each choice into the review, after the first build. Three
  choices:
  - **The "here" outline stays two boxes:** the turn's last edge and its label (the game's judgement cell, or a
    variation's label) each show "here". The other choice was one box round both. The reason: "B [one box] can be
    misunderstood". One box round both could read as one move.
  - **A variation's turn label is the turn's own element.** The first build put the turn's label, its "…" and its ◆
    in the button of the move that ends the turn. The reason: "Making it part of a move makes it seem like the
    move's label, instead of the turn's." Now they are their own button after the turn's last edge, as the game's
    judgement cell. It acts as that edge: pointing at it previews the edge's line, a click goes there, and a
    right-click opens the edge's menu. One function gives both buttons these actions (`asBranch`, as `asMove` on the
    game's line). Its state is the edge's "here" and picked, and it is no `.mv`, so the place on screen is still one
    move. Its title is the turn's tooltip. A turn with no label, no "…" and no ◆ has no such button. By edge nothing
    changes: the label is the edge's own, in its button.
  - **The pointer on a turn's label lights the whole turn.** The request: "So for edge mode: edge and labels is one
    element. For turn mode: edge is its own element. But when hovering over label, both moves and label treat as one
    element." The page with the group drawn in was then approved. By turn, the pointer on a turn's label (a
    variation's button, or the game's judgement cell) lights the turn's edges in the label's row and the label as one
    group. One outline goes round them, in the pointer's style of the row's form (`GROUP_HOVER` in the text form and
    on the game's line, the ink outline in pills and dots). The members' own pointer outlines do not show then, and the
    "here" and picked outlines stay. Pointing at one edge lights that edge alone. A turn that wraps lights each line's
    part. A variation that starts in a turn's middle lights only the turn's edges in the label's row.
- **How the group is drawn:** an overlay (`lightsTurn` in `ReviewView.svelte`, an attachment on each turn's label).
  When a pointer that hovers comes onto a turn's label, the view measures the label and the row's elements that act
  as the turn's edges. It draws one box for each line that holds them, behind the row's content: the row is
  `isolate`, and the box is at a negative z-index. The other means do not fit. A wrapper round the turn's edges and
  its label would be one flex item, and would change how the row wraps. A row element holds several turns in a
  variation. `:has()` can style each member, but cannot draw one outline round several items and the gaps between
  them, on each line.
- **The group while the pointer stays:** a `ResizeObserver` on the row and its elements measures the group again
  when one of them changes size. A "…" becomes a label, a label becomes the book mark when its part of the book
  loads, a ◆ comes, or the list gets narrower. A `MutationObserver` adds each element that comes into the row to the
  watch: one that comes before the members moves them. A group measured only when the pointer came would cut through
  the new label. The boxes render with their label, and the group goes out when the label goes from under the pointer. A
  turn whose "…" ends in a label that the list does not show (Best, Excellent or Good, with no ◆) loses its button.
  A removed element gets no `mouseleave`, so a group that only `mouseleave` cleared would stay lit, and the board
  would keep the label's preview, until the pointer passed over another label. The label's preview ends with it.
- **A touch lights no group.** Tailwind's `hover:` applies only where the device can hover, so a tap on a move does
  not leave its pointer outline. A tap sends `mouseenter` too, so a group that started on it would stay lit after
  the tap, until the next tap elsewhere. The group starts on `pointerenter`, and not for a touch. The preview that a
  long press leaves stays abscls-3wp0's.
- **Measured (the design by turn)** in headless Chromium at 1366 × 900, on K12-N11 before and after "Evaluate quality".
  By turn, the move's button keeps its size (text 62.3 × 21 px, pills 17 × 17.4 px, dots 13.4 × 13.4 px), and the
  turn's own button after it is 20.7 × 19.1 px in the text form and 16.5 × 16.6 px in pills and dots. The rows keep
  their height: 25 px in the text form, 21.4 px in pills and 21.1 px in dots. By edge the sizes are those of the first
  build. With the pointer on the turn's label, one box lights the move and the label: in the text form a fill and a
  1 px line in the line colour, in pills and dots a 1 px ink outline, behind the row's content.
- **Tests (the design by turn):** `tests/book-review.spec.ts`, in text, pills and dots. By turn, K12-N11's book mark
  is in the turn's own button, outside the move's button. That button previews the move's line, goes there, opens
  its menu, and takes "here" and picked. The turn N11-Q10 K12-N11 starts on the game's line: the pointer on its
  label lights K12-N11 and the label, not the game's N11-Q10. On the review file with two variations, the pointer on
  the label of D10-G9 D9-G11 lights both edges and the label in one box. The test reads each box's computed outline
  (solid, 1 px), and checks that the members' own outlines do not show. The pointer on one edge lights that edge
  alone. A row made narrow, so that the label wraps, lights two boxes. On the game's line, the pointer on turn 2's
  cell lights N11-Q10, O11-Q10 and the cell, not A10-D9. By edge, the label lights no group. In each form, by edge
  and by turn, the row has the same height before and after "Evaluate quality". In each form, the label grows while
  the pointer stays on it, and the group grows with it. An element put into the row before the turn's edges moves
  them, and the group moves with them. A tap on the label, in a page with touch, sends the mouse events of a tap, goes
  to the move and lights no group.

### Drawing Board's notes (2026-11-02)

abscls-8tl1.16. Design 33, "The player's notes", gives the result. What the issue left open, and why:

- **Hedge School's notes logic moved to `packages/review`** (`notes.ts` and its test, by `git mv`), with the notes'
  colour tokens (`review.css`). The two boards share the board's colours, so the notes' 3:1 against the board holds
  on both. Hedge School's notes do what they did. Its unit test moved unchanged, and its board, view and Practice
  take the same functions from the package. `brushFor` now reads a site's table of keys. So a new unit test checks
  Hedge School's colour for each of the 16 sets of keys held, against chessground's rule. A new browser test
  (`tests/notes.spec.ts`) checks Hedge School's notes on Practice's board: a ring, a line, the colours by its keys,
  the same note again, a left click that clears them, and the notes by position. Before it, no browser test covered
  them.
- **Notes on the board only.** The hands' cells are in each blueprint's frame, which a line and an edit change. A note
  there would need another kind of note, and could outlive its cell.
- **An arrow between touching hexes is a note,** as on Lichess. The tip stops 0.2 short of the centre, and the head is
  0.66 long. So the shaft still shows between touching hexes (0.87).
- **A highlighted hex is a ring and a fill.** The fill goes under the cells, and the ring over everything, with a halo
  in the board's colour. A cell keeps its owner's colour, and the note reads on a cell of either player.
- **The notes hide while a preview shows another position,** as in Hedge School's view, which then gives the board no
  notes. A candidate's line on the position on screen keeps them.
- **A click clears the notes, and a pan does not.** Chessground clears the shapes on any press of the left button.
  Hedge School's board does not pan, so a press there is a click. Drawing Board's board pans with the left button. A
  pan that cleared the notes would lose them each time the player moved the board.
- **Drawing Board's own keys.** Shift with a right drag highlights each hex that the drag goes across, as
  strategyjam.org's Sandbox does ("Shift+right-drag: highlight hexes" in its help). A hex is an area, and a group of
  hexes is a usual note on this board. Ctrl alone gives yellow, so Shift is free for the drag. A drag whose first hex
  has a highlight of its colour clears that colour's highlights instead. So the same drag again removes what it drew,
  as a second right-click does, with no key for an eraser. Hedge School's notes are at points, and its keys stay:
  Shift or Ctrl for yellow. Each site gives its keys as one table (`BrushKeys` in `notes.ts`). Its board reads the
  table to choose the colour, and its list of keys and clicks shows the table, so the two cannot differ.
  strategyjam.org's Sandbox has three colours (yellow, green and purple), chosen by a button or a key.
- **A drag off the board on screen takes no hex,** as chessground drops a shape that is released off its board. Off
  the board is outside the field or under the hands' panel, where the player cannot see the hex. An arrow released
  there is no note.
- **An arrow keeps its direction** (from the audit of the open issues, abscls-70t7). Chessground's
  `sameEndpoints` counts a shape from B to A as another shape than the one from A to B. Drawing Board's arrow has a
  head, so it takes that rule: an arrow drawn back over an arrow is a second arrow, and does not remove the first or
  change its colour. Hedge School's line has no head, and keeps its rule (`sameNote`): the line drawn the other way
  is the same line. `toggleNote` takes the site's rule, with Hedge School's by default. A unit test checks each rule.
- **What a fast drag of highlights takes.** `hexesAlong` takes the hex under points of the stroke at most a tenth of
  a hex's radius apart. So it misses no hex that the stroke crosses for a tenth of the radius or more, however far
  apart the pointer's two moves are. It can leave out a hex whose corner the stroke only clips: the player did not
  mean that hex. A unit test draws a stroke 30 radii long, 0.03 of a radius past a row of 17 corners: it takes each
  of the 17 hexes, which it crosses for 0.104 of the radius. Points 0.12 apart or more leave some out. A stroke 0.01
  past a corner crosses its hex for 0.035, and leaves it out.
- **Notes need a mouse.** A touch screen has no right button, and no gesture for a note, as on Hedge School's board
  and Lichess's. The layout test of the board with notes draws them with a mouse at 1,376 × 952 and then sets the
  window to the other sizes, 390 × 844 too: it checks the layout, not touch.
- **Firefox and Shift.** In Firefox, a right-click with Shift opens the browser's own menu with no event
  `contextmenu` for the page to cancel (MDN, "Element: contextmenu event"). A right drag with Shift can then end with
  Firefox's menu on screen, and the page cannot stop it. Ctrl and Alt do not open it. The sites are tested in Chromium
  only.

### `btn-danger` moves to the practice package (2026-11-04)

abscls-8tl1.21.

- **The fault:** Drawing Board's Practice confirms Abort and Resign with a button of class `btn-danger`, but the
  utility was defined only in Hedge School's `src/app.css`. In Drawing Board the button had no fill, no border colour
  and no white text. The move of the review's styles (2026-10-26) kept `btn-danger` in Hedge School's `app.css`,
  because no package used it. That is still true, but now each site uses it, so the two sites need one definition.
- **The place:** `packages/practice/src/practice.css`. Both sites import it, and the practice package already depends
  on the view's package, so the utility keeps `--blunder-fill` (review.css) and its declarations do not change.
  `site.css` would need a token of its own with the same two values, because the site package must not read the
  view's tokens. Two copies of one colour can drift apart. The cost of the choice: Hedge School's ConfirmDialog (a
  game's Delete on the review's home, and the Delete of the practice games on the Privacy page) is outside Practice.
  It gets the utility through the site's import of `practice.css`.
- **Checked:** Hedge School's built CSS has the same two rules of `btn-danger` (plain and `:not(:disabled)`) with the
  same declarations. Drawing Board's built CSS now has the plain rule. It has no `:not(:disabled)` rule, because no
  page of Drawing Board's uses that variant. Two browser tests (`tests/drawingboard-practice.spec.ts`) assert the
  fill, the border and the text colour in both themes. One opens the confirm step of Abort and of Resign in a game.
  It runs only when Drawing Board's build has the practice bot (`npm run engine` before the build). The other adds a
  `btn-danger` button to a page, and the Tests workflow runs it.

### Blueprints' site is Cyanotype (2026-11-04)

abscls-8tl1.23.

- **The decision:** Blueprints' site is named **Cyanotype**, in place of Drawing Board. The reason: Drawing Board
  could name many other games ("It's so generic it can be applied to many other games", then "yes, Cyanotype"). A
  cyanotype is the printing process that made blueprints: white lines on Prussian blue, so the name belongs to
  Blueprints alone. The engine and its practice bot keep the name Stamp Duty.
- **The whole name changes now,** the internal names too: the folder `apps/cyanotype`, the package `cyanotype`, the
  storage keys (`cyanotype:…`), the userscript's files (`/cyanotype.user.js`, `/cyanotype.meta.js`), the deploy job
  `cyanotype`, the repository variable `CYANOTYPE_PAGES_PROJECT` and the tests' `CYANOTYPE_BASE_URL`. No release
  exists yet, so no visitor keeps a game, a setting or an installed userscript under the old names, and the change
  needs no migration.
- **The address:** `cyanotype.abstractclass.org`, from the Pages project `cyanotype`. `cyanotype.pages.dev` belongs
  to another site, so the project is at `cyanotype-ztp.pages.dev`. The deploy job built a preview's address as
  `<branch>.<project>.pages.dev`, which would have sent a preview's userscript to the other site. It now reads the
  host from the project in Cloudflare's API (`subdomain`) before the build, with the deploy's token, and fails when
  the API gives none (docs/hosting.md, section 9). The build needs the address, so Wrangler's deploy output, which
  comes after the build, cannot give it. A repository variable for the host would only repeat the API's answer.
- **The site's text:** the home page's heading and the About page's paragraph on the names played on the old name.
  They now tell of the cyanotype.
- **History:** the earlier entries of this log, and the requests to the engine repository, keep the name Drawing
  Board. There, Drawing Board is Cyanotype.

### Openings, the book's own page, on the test book (2026-11-04)

abscls-tpaj.12. Openings (`/openings`) is built, as design 32 decides (items 2, 5 and 13), on the test book.

- **The page:** the Analysis board's layout and controls (ReviewView in its board form), with a board of its own

  browser keeps no choice for it. The board takes the book's area map at each book position (`GameAnalysis.maps`), so

  engine's settings with the engine off there. The engine header says "The engine waits at a book position. To
  search, select Candidates." The test book's searches have 512 visits, so the reason "the book is deeper" holds only
  for the engine's book (abscls-tpaj.13).
- **The tree** (`src/lib/book/tree.ts`): the main line is `mainLine` of the sentences. Each other book move hangs under
  the move before it, folded under a chevron button that says how many moves it holds ("2 other book moves instead
  of A10-D9") and whether it is open (`aria-expanded`). An open fold adds each move's line to the board: the move, a
  trap's refutation, then the best book moves to the end of the move's main line. A book move played from the table
  adds its line the same way. A line stops after a move that reaches a position by another way than its canonical
  parent, with the link "Continues in …".
- **The choices that design 32 left open:**
  - **The folds are kept for the visit only,** not in the address. The address names a position (design 22), and the
    page takes it out of the address at once, for the analytics. The path to the position on screen is always open,
    so a reload at the same position shows the same line. The lines that a fold added stay on the kept board.
  - **"Continues in" names the canonical line's last turn,** in the notation, with "the main line" where it is on the
    main line: "Continues in the main line, 2. N11-Q10 L10-N11", or "Continues in 2. N11-Q10 O11-Q10". The turn is
    what the player reads in the move list, and the link goes there. A turn's two edges in the other order end with
    this link. "Also reached by" lists only the move orders across turns, as design 32 says.
  - **"Back to the main line" is in the step bar,** beside "Open in Analysis", on every width. On a phone the bar is
    fixed to the window's foot, so the way back is in view whenever the board is. There the two take their short
    words ("Main line", "Analysis"), so that the bar keeps two rows. Their full words stay their names.
  - **While the start's part loads,** the page shows the board's skeleton until the engine's rules are ready, as the
    Analysis board does. Then the board shows at once, and the table says "Loading the book…" (item 11) until the
    start's part loads. The first view's box says "Loading the book…" until the main line's parts load, and the main
    line then comes into the move list. A book that does not load leaves the board without a main line, with the
    table's "Try again".
- **The build:** Openings, its header tab and "Study in Openings" are in the early edition, and only in a build that
  the dev or preview server serves with the test book (`VITE_TEST_BOOK`, set by `vite.config.ts` where
  `CF_PAGES_BRANCH` is not set). The deploy's builds are early-edition builds too, and they serve no test book, so
  `VITE_EDITION` alone would have put a page with no book on the live site. A build without the early edition has no
  `/openings` page and no fourth tab.
- **The entry points:** "Study in Openings" under the sentence of the book's table, in the review and on the Analysis
  board, where the path starts at the book's start. "Open in Analysis" in Openings' step bar: the path as a record,
  at its end, with `via=openings`, which the board counts as neither an import nor a load.
- **The move list's current item:** the move of the position on screen has `aria-current="location"`, on every board
  page.
- **The counts (design 17):** `openings_open` with `openings_from`, `openings_positions` at 5, 10, 25 and 50 positions
  in a visit, and the features `book shown`, `fold opened` and `back to main line`. The refutations played were
  counted already (`book refutation played`): design 17 now lists them.
- **Tests with players are no release gate.** The answer in the audit abscls-70t7 (2026-11-04): "no release gate".
  The five players a task (abscls-tpaj.10) are a first round that finds problems. Design 32, "Consequences", says so.
- **Tests:** `src/lib/book/tree.test.ts` on both test books (the main line, a book move's line, a trap's refutation,
  the canonical link, the move orders across turns, a mirror image, the folds' words). `tests/openings.spec.ts` in
  Chromium, with the engine off but in one test: the fourth tab and the first view, a fold, a trap and its
  refutation, a move order's link, a mirror image, the way back, "Open in Analysis" and "Study in Openings", the
  keyboard only, the phone's layout and a tap, and the engine that waits at a book position and starts with
  "Candidates", on the CPU. `tests/layout.spec.ts` sweeps `/openings` with a fold open, and checks its step bar on a
  phone.
- **Not built:** the win chance bar above the board says "not analyzed yet" at a book position while the engine
  waits: it reads the engine's search only.

### Openings after a look: no main line's box, a steady sentence, the way back to where the path left (2026-11-04)

abscls-tpaj.12, the review of the page that the entry before records. A look at the built page on the test book gave
the first three changes. The review found the others. Design 32 gives the result.

- **No box of the main line in the first view.** The box gave the main line, one turn a line, each with its sentence.
  The reason, from the look: "'The main line' text box doesn't seem particularly useful, to be honest. It doesn't give
  any insight at the moment. I guess we don't have enough concept knowledge in the game to say things other than this
  line, that line, who is better after what." The first view is now the table and the move list, whose main line is
  the line to learn. Design 32 lists the box under "Alternatives": it can come back when the book can name ideas, and
  not only lines and win chances. `mainLine` in `sentences.ts` stays, for the move list's main line. Its turns'
  sentences (`lineTurn`) now have no reader but their unit test.
- **The sentence under the table keeps its height.** It changed height as the pointer went over the rows, so the move
  list under it jumped. The table now puts every book row's sentence in one grid cell and shows only the current one,
  so the slot keeps the height of the position's tallest sentence. A fixed height would cut a long sentence or leave a
  gap under a short one. The sentence is a band of the table, in a lit row's tint under the table's last row, with a
  rule under it, so it reads as a part of the table. The move list starts after it, under its own rule. The review,
  the Analysis board and Openings share the table, so the change holds on all three.
- **"Back to the main line" goes where the path left the main line:** the last position of the path on the main line.
  It went to the main line after as many edges as the position on screen, a position that the player may never have
  seen. The path's own edges count, not the positions that they reach: a move order or a mirror image that reaches a
  position of the main line left the main line at its first edge that differs.
- **The engine header with the switch off** says what it says on the Analysis board. It said "The engine waits at a
  book position" with the switch off. The page's note (`engineNote` in ReviewView) now shows only while the switch is
  on. While the engine waits, the threat's line and a move asked to evaluate give the same note, in the place of "the
  engine is off", which they said while the switch was on.
- **The win chance above the board is the book's at a book position,** as the table's title row gives it. It said "not
  analyzed yet" while the engine waited. The analysis takes the book's values for its view as an option
  (`AnalysisOptions.viewValues`: the area map and the win chance), in the place of `GameAnalysis.maps`. They give no
  label.
- **The area map is on at each visit.** Openings used the Analysis board's choice of the map, so a player who turned
  the map off there had it off on Openings, against design 32, item 5. The page now keeps no choice of the map, and
  the Analysis board's choice stays as it is.
- **The trap and the other move order** stay as they were built: "trap and another move order are fine".
- **The main line ends where the book's main line ends.** A line played from its end, or a fold opened there ("3 book
  moves after G12-J15"), made the board's main line longer, as the Analysis board does, and the page kept the longer
  line at each visit. The analysis now takes `AnalysisOptions.fixedMain`: such lines are variations. The move list
  had no place for a variation from the main line's end, as a turn's band holds the lines from the positions before
  its edges: a band after the last turn now holds them, with the fold there first.
- **The engine searches where a part of the book did not load.** It waited there, with the table's "The book did not
  load", against design 32, item 11.
- **"Also reached by" goes to its line.** Its links did nothing: the page never gave the place its way to a line.
  `OpeningsPlace` now takes it in its constructor.
- **Simpler code, the same behaviour:**
  - The shared analysis takes the board's form as an option (`AnalysisOptions.board`). `OPENINGS_ID` is in
    `src/lib/game/store.ts`, so the shared packages name no page of Hedge School.
  - A fold gives its moves (`MoveFold.at`), and the move list asks it once a position. A closed fold keeps the path's
    moves by a string of their keys, so the move list's rows do not run again at each step.
  - The link "Continues in" knows at once from the book's positions where it shows, and finds only its words later.
  - Openings' table is the review's table with its own line under the title row (`lead`). Its place counts no
    feature: the switch's `book shown` is for the review and the Analysis board.
  - "Also reached by" asks the book again only when the path's positions change, not at each result of the engine.
  - A fold's lines are found together, then added. The book's main line loads while the engine does.
  - A brought record's line comes from `boardOfRecord` (`src/lib/game/board.ts`), as on the Analysis board.
  - `positionsAlong` in `tree.ts` walks a line through the book, for the page and the unit tests.
- **Tests:** `tests/openings.spec.ts` checks that the first view has no box, the book's win chance above the board,
  the engine header with the switch off, the area map at each visit with the Analysis board's map off, and the way
  back at A10-D9 O11-Q10 N11-Q10 (to A10-D9, where the fold closes again), after D10-G9 and after the mirror image
  A10-D11 (to the start), and a move played at the end of the book's main line, which stays a variation in the move
  list. `tests/layout.spec.ts` checks that the move list's top, from the table's top, does not move while the
  pointer, then the focus, goes over each row of the book's table: on Openings and the Analysis board, by edge and
  by turn, at 1,400 and 360 pixels wide, and in the review by edge and by turn at 360 and 1,400 pixels wide.
- **Not changed, for a later issue:** while the engine waits at a book position, the session pauses the whole engine,
  so a move asked to evaluate and the threat wait too, with the note that says why. Only the search of the position
  on screen needs to wait. The design files in `docs/ux/book-explorer/` still describe the box: they are the design's
  working files, and design 32 rules where they differ.

### Cyanotype's review takes two moves that give one position as one move (2026-11-05)

Design 33, item 9, built (abscls-8tl1.19): two of Blueprints' moves with different names that give one position are
one move in the review.

- **How often on the review's test game** (`apps/cyanotype/src/lib/review/fixtures/stamp-duty.txt`): the engine
  searched each of the game's 120 positions at 512 visits on the CPU (engine-70dfdc0f, network
  b6c96-s22323968-d845223), as the review searches at Lite. The engine's describe gave the position after each
  candidate and after each legal move.
  - Turns 1 to 20, the positions that the browser test reviews (0 to 38): 728 candidates, and no two of them give one
    position. The move played never gives a candidate's position under another name. Only positions 0 and 1 have
    two legal moves that give one position: 35 pairs each, a placement of blueprint 1 and of blueprint 3, which are
    equal at the start.
  - The whole game: 2,075 candidates in 120 positions, and one pair that gives one position. At position 83 the
    engine's first choice `1:0,0>1:2,-1` (76 visits, Blue 15.3%) and its fourth choice `1:1,0>1:-1,1` (16 visits, Blue
    12.9%) give one hand. Each moves one cell of blueprint 1, a star with a plain cell. The search gave the two moves
    the same line after them, but values of their own. The move played never gives a candidate's position under
    another name. 62 positions have such legal moves: 125,322 legal moves give 124,984 positions. At position 87,
    the move played (`1:0,0>1:2,-1`) has a twin among the legal moves, which the search there did not list.
  - A second run on positions 0 to 38 and 83, with the same engine, network and visits, gave the same counts: 728
    candidates and no pair on turns 1 to 20, and the same pair at position 83. Its first choice there had 86 visits.
- **Each place that compares two moves of one position**, and what went wrong with two names for one position:
  - The candidates (`distinctCandidates`): two rows of the table and two ranks on the board for one move. The engine's
    second choice (`secondChoice`, `onlyMove`) could be the first choice's twin, so a Great's gap read 0.
  - Their twins (`twinsOf`) and a candidate's rank (`rankOf`): the twin was a candidate of its own.
  - The labels (`sameMove` in `judgeBranchMove` and the review's edges, `judgeTurn` and its `sameTurn`,
    `otherCandidate`, the Greats' checks in the analysis): a move that gives the first choice's position under another
    name was not Best, and a Great's other candidate could be the played move's twin.
  - The move list's note "… was best" (`shortNote`): it named the engine's choice for a move that gives its position.
  - The game's tree: such a move made a variation beside the game's move, and its position was searched again.
  - A line's steps (`stepsOf`) and the turn's marks on the board (`ReviewBoard.svelte`): these compare a line with
    the line whose steps came, and a mark with the moves that it marks. A name that differs gets its steps from the
    engine again. The board shows the same position.
  - Not changed, still by name: the engine's best line under a Mistake's or a Blunder's note follows the game's line
    only by the moves' names. The listed line marks its moves played in the tree by their names too. A Great's
    confirmation searches the position after the second choice by its name. A turn in the other order compares by
    names (design 29, item 9).
- **The cost of each place,** measured in Node on the test game's positions 0, 1, 20, 42, 83 and 100:
  - The site's key of the position after a move (`afterKey`): 5.2 to 9.9 µs for an edit, 1.3 to 3.1 µs for a
    placement.
  - The game's `equal` with the position: two keys, 10 to 20 µs a comparison. The table's twins compare each
    candidate with each: 400 comparisons for 20 candidates, about 5 ms at each render.
  - A key of the position in the tree from the engine (its describe of the position after the move): 0.8 to 3.1 ms a
    move, in the engine's worker.
  - The twins of one analysis by the key (`withTwins`), with the position's candidates (4 to 21) and the move played:
    17 to 133 µs, once for each analysis and moves.
- **The choice: the game's key of the position after a move, and twins.** The game interface takes an optional
  `afterKey(move, before)`. The shared analysis gives each analysis with its twins (`analysisOf` and `data`, which the
  view reads too). There, `withTwins` makes a candidate that gives an earlier candidate's position its twin. A move of
  the tree that gives a candidate's position under another name becomes a twin too. The tree takes a move that gives
  a tree move's position along that move (the shared analysis's `nodesOf`, with `sameNodes`).
  - Every comparison of the list gives one answer: each reads the analysis's candidates and their twins, as the
    review already reads Enclosure's symmetric twins. `equal` with the position would leave `distinctCandidates`,
    `secondChoice` and `onlyMove` wrong, because they take no position.
  - One interface: Enclosure gives no key, and `equal` keeps its meaning and its tests. Hedge School's analyses come
    back as they are.
  - Simplest: of the model's functions, only `sameTurn` takes more: the turn's two analyses. In the turn's order, it
    takes only the twins by position (`samePosition`), not Enclosure's symmetric twins. After a symmetric twin, the
    position is the mirror image, so the engine's second edge is another edge there. A first version took both, and
    then labelled Best an Enclosure turn of the first choice's mirror image and the line's second edge.
  - Cost: the key is in the site, 100 to 500 times faster than the engine's describe, and synchronous. The twins of an
    analysis are kept, so a page that derives them again pays nothing.
- **The key** (`src/lib/review/blueprints.ts`): for an edit, the mover's hand after it, with the two blueprints back
  in their frames (`handAfter`). For a placement, its footprint. On the test game's positions 0 and 83, the keys
  group all 2,090 legal moves as the engine's positions after them do (`blueprints.engine.test.ts`).
- **The table's mark ⇅** names Blueprints' twins "Same position" (the view's `twinWords`). Cyanotype's name fills its
  cell, so a row with twins leaves room for the mark.
- **What changes on the page:** on turns 1 to 20, nothing changes. At position 83, the table has three rows in place of
  four, with ⇅ on the first choice, and the hand's panel shows rank 1 on both edits. The screenshots, before and
  after: the Analysis board at position 83, at 512 visits, 1,376 by 952 pixels, in headless Chromium.
- **Tests:** `src/lib/review/twins.test.ts` in Cyanotype, on position 83: the key, the table's rows, the rank, the
  label, a turn's label, the note, the other candidate, a twin from the tree and the tree's node. Without the change,
  four of its five tests fail. The analysis package's `game.test.ts` and `tree.test.ts` check `withTwins`, the shared
  analysis's twins and tree nodes (`nodesOf`), a turn in the engine's order with a twin of each kind, and
  `sameNodes` on the packages' test game.

### The signs of After vs before by good and bad: a green plus, a yellow minus (2026-11-04)

abscls-8fe7. The proposal: the signs of the area map's style "After vs before" take colours that are not the players',
by good and bad for the player who chose, for both sides. A green plus is good for that player, and a yellow minus is
bad. Each sign took a side's colour: a plus the colour of the player who chose, a minus the enemy's. So a blue minus
read as "Blue lost here", where it meant that the point moved toward Blue, which was bad for Red, the player who chose.
The colour and the shape said two things, and the colour won. KaTrain's loss grid draws its losses in one colour of its
evaluation scale, whichever side moved, so the change moves back toward KaTrain. The entry of 2026-10-21, "The marks of
After vs before, and 0.05", gave the players' colours for one colour language on the board. Green and yellow are the
labels' colours for good and inaccurate, so the signs now speak the labels' language, and that reason turns around.
Hedge School and Cyanotype take one rule. Design 30 gives the result.

- **The colours** are two tokens in `packages/review/src/review.css`, `--sign-green` and `--sign-yellow`. The boards
  and the legend draw a sign in them, and the setting's explanation names them, from one name each (`SIGN_COLOUR`,
  `signInk` and `DIFFERENCE_HELP` in `ownership.ts`). The two sites share the board's colours: #f3ead7 in the light
  theme, #3a362e in the dark theme. The contrasts (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11, at least 3:1):

  | Sign | Theme | Colour | Board | Blue cell or edge | Red cell or edge | Blue region | Red region |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Green | Light | #4f8830, Excellent's ink | 3.59:1 | 1.10:1 | 1.05:1 | 2.94:1 | 2.94:1 |
  | Yellow | Light | #9e7706, Inaccuracy's hue darker | 3.45:1 | 1.15:1 | 1.09:1 | 2.83:1 | 2.83:1 |
  | Green | Dark | #6faa52, Excellent's fill | 4.32:1 | 1.14:1 | 1.18:1 | 3.52:1 | 3.57:1 |
  | Yellow | Dark | #d9a521, Inaccuracy's fill | 5.35:1 | 1.41:1 | 1.47:1 | 4.36:1 | 4.42:1 |

  A region is the player's colour at 0.16 over the board. The candidate yellow, Inaccuracy's ink #bc8d07, is 2.53:1 on
  the light board, so the light theme takes its hue darker. The labels' Good green (#6f935a in the light theme) is
  2.93:1 there. Excellent's green is the lightest of the labels' greens that passes in both themes.
- **The halo stays.** Its colour is the board's, so a sign keeps its contrast against the board wherever it lies. No
  green or yellow passes against a cell or an edge, and on the light board none passes against a region: the table
  shows 1.05:1 to 2.94:1 there. The halo against a cell or an edge is 3.95:1 (Blue) and 3.77:1 (Red) in the light
  theme, and 3.80:1 and 3.65:1 in the dark theme.
- **The shapes stay,** the plus and the minus, so that the colour is not the only cue (1.4.1). Green against yellow
  is 1.04:1 in the light theme and 1.24:1 in the dark theme: a red-green colour-blind player reads the shapes.
- **The text.** The explanation of "Area map style" says "A green plus shows a rise: good for that player. A yellow
  minus shows a fall: bad for that player." in the place of the sentences about the players' colours. The two sites
  share the style's whole explanation (`DIFFERENCE_HELP`). The legend's two signs take the same colours.
- **Cyanotype offers no area map yet** (its design 33, "No area map yet"). Its board and its kept explanation
  (`AREA_MAP`) take the rule, for when it does.

### Cyanotype's engine from Blueprints' first release (2026-11-05)

Design 33, "The engine's files", changed (abscls-8tl1.24): Cyanotype takes every engine file from Blueprints' first
release, `engine-3ac5c2fc` (Stamp Duty 0.1), in the public repository `abstractclass-org/blueprints-engine`. The
engine repository's record of the release is its `docs/decisions/organization.md`, entry of 2026-11-05.

- **The lock** (`apps/cyanotype/engine.lock.json`): seven files, each from the release (a source of kind `release`),
  with the SHA-256 and the size of the release's manifest. The module `blueprints-engine.wasm` (1,518,637 bytes,
  protocol 0.7.1, build and search `3ac5c2fc`), `gpu_engine.mjs`, `practice_bot.mjs`, the practice bot
  `blueprints-bot.wasm` (1,787,252 bytes, interface 0.1.2), `NOTICES.txt`, `LICENSE.txt`, and bpj5's network
  `b6c96-s40806528-d2304635` (2,228,327 bytes), whose name is Stamp Duty 0.1. The release's `settings.cfg` is the
  text of the search's settings, which the module embeds: the site does not read it, and the lock does not take it.
  `npm run engine -- --deploy` fetched the seven files, each with the lock's SHA-256, and the module answered protocol
  0.7.1 and the search `3ac5c2fc`, as the lock gives.
- **The fixtures:** `npm run fixtures` wrote `src/lib/board/fixtures.json` again from the release. Only its header
  changed: the five games have the same positions, legal moves and effects.
- **Two moves that give one position:** at position 83 of the review's test game, the release's network at 512 visits
  gives three candidates (`1@3,-3`, `2@-1,6`, `2@21,19`), and no two of them give one position. The earlier network's
  pair (`1:0,0>1:2,-1` and `1:1,0>1:-1,1`) came again with the earlier build and the same script, with the recorded
  values. `twins.test.ts` does not run the engine: it keeps that pair, a real reply of `engine-70dfdc0f`, as its case.
- **The bot's name on Practice:** the network now has a release name that names Stamp Duty, so the name is the
  network's alone, "Stamp Duty 0.1, 64 visits, Low variety", as Hedge School names HedgeFund's. A network without a
  release name keeps "Stamp Duty (its id)".
- **CI:** the step `cyanotype-engine` of `npm run check:all` fetches the files before Cyanotype's checks, and stops
  them when it fails. The Tests workflow keeps Cyanotype's downloads in a cache of their own, by the lock, and its
  Windows job fetches them before Cyanotype's build. So the Cyanotype tests that need the engine run there. In CI, a
  Cyanotype preview with no engine files now fails the review's and Practice's browser tests, in place of a skip that
  would pass with no sign.
- **The Tests workflow's time limits:** 75 minutes for the Linux job and 60 for the Windows job, from 40. On this
  computer at 2 threads, the browser tests (`npm run test:layout -- --project=chromium`, 153 tests: 148 passed and 5
  skipped) took 53.5 minutes, about 35 of them in Cyanotype's engine tests: the review of the test game twice (about
  14 minutes in `cyanotype-review.spec.ts` before its tests, and 16.9 in the layout test's review) and the two practice
  games (4.1). The same tests without Cyanotype's engine took 14 minutes in the last CI run before this change. So the
  Linux job would pass 40 minutes. No CI run has measured it yet.
- **The deploy:** the job `cyanotype` names the Pages project `cyanotype`, as the site's job names `hedgeschool`, and
  has no `if:`. The repository variable `CYANOTYPE_PAGES_PROJECT` only kept the job off until the project existed. It
  fetches the release's files before its checks and its build. `docs/hosting.md` section 9 gives the owner's steps:
  no variable, and the first live deployment from the job at a release, not from a local build. Cloudflare's guide to
  custom domains names no deployment that must come before a domain. The domain `cyanotype.abstractclass.org` was
  added on 2026-11-05, before any deployment: it answers with status 522 until the first production deployment, and
  then serves it.
- **The quality labels change with the network.** The review of the test game's turns 1 to 20 at Lite (512 visits),
  in headless Chromium on the CPU, with the earlier build's files and with the release's: by move, 22 of 39 quality
  labels changed. By turn, the display's default, 14 of 20 changed. One review of each, so search noise is part of the
