### The engine step: one release of the lock names every file (2026-11-10)

- **Decided** (abscls-8tl1.84): the check of each lock as one release's set changes its rule. One release of the lock
  must name every file of the lock from a release, with the lock's SHA-256 and size (`checkOneReleaseSet` in
  `packages/engine/src/lock-check.ts`, design 03). The earlier rule was "each file has the entry of the newest of the
  lock's releases that names it". It ordered the releases by the `Last-Modified` time of each manifest's download.
  The cache kept that time beside each manifest (`releases/<tag>/manifest.time`). The step no longer reads or keeps
  that time.
- **Why:** the rule needs no order of the releases, so it needs no time.
  - Upload order is not release order. A manifest that is uploaded again to an earlier release, to correct it, made
    that release the newest, and the old rule then refused a correct lock. The new rule reads no time, so such a
    manifest changes nothing.
  - A warm cache with no `manifest.time` downloaded every manifest again. The new rule reads the cached manifests
    only, so a warm cache reads no network (`packages/engine/src/release-manifests.ts`).
  - A release of an earlier commit that changes only the terms, after a release of a later commit, is the limit
    that both rules share. A lock with those terms and the later commit's modules has no release that names all its
    files, so the new rule refuses it too. Such a release must name the later files, or come from the later commit.
  - The new rule refuses a lock that keeps a file that its newest release dropped. The old rule passed such a file
    with its own release's entry.
- **The message:** when no release names every file, the step names the release that names the most files, and
  each file that it does not name, with the lock's entry and the release's (or "no entry").
- **A limit of the cache:** the step downloads a cached manifest again only when it does not give the lock's entries
  for its own release's files. A manifest that is uploaded again to a release after the cache took it stays as the
  cache has it. On a machine, delete `releases/<tag>` from the download cache to read it again. On CI, the cache
  changes with the lock.
- **On CI:** the Tests workflow keeps each lock's download cache by the lock's hash. When the key finds a cache,
  actions/cache does not save it again. The caches saved before the check of the release's set hold no manifests.
  The four keys now start with `engine-v2-` and `cyanotype-engine-v2-`, so each job saves a new cache with the
  manifests once.
- **The review** made the step refuse a manifest that is JSON but not a manifest (a number, a list, or `assets`
  that is not a list), with the release's name. A cached one of that form downloads again. A download that stops
  before the end of its file stops the step with the release and the URL.
- **Checked:** both locks pass on their releases: engine-c43233eb names all 19 files of Hedge School's lock, and
  engine-887be290 all 13 of Cyanotype's. With an empty cache, each step downloaded the manifests of the lock's
  releases once (5 and 2). Run again with a fetch that a script made fail, both steps passed from the cache. With no
  cached manifests, no network, HTTP 504 and HTTP 403 each stopped the step with the release, the URL and the cause.
  Hedge School's lock with engine-d6786eba's `enclosure-eval.wasm` stopped the step: the closest release,
  engine-c43233eb, gives that file another SHA-256. Cyanotype's lock with engine-3ac5c2fc's `LICENSE.txt` stopped it
  the same way, with engine-887be290 as the closest. The unit tests use fake manifests in the real manifests' shape,
  and a fake download for the cache.

### Practice's tests keep their storage before the page's code runs (2026-11-10)

Beads abscls-z0jz. Two cases of `cyanotype-practice.spec.ts` each failed once in the whole suite under the machine's
load. In both, the Practice page showed no content after a load.

- **The dropped-game case** ("a kept game whose network the site does not ship gives way to the settings card"):
  `page.goto` returns at the load event, and the page's code runs after it. In 30 of 30 loads of `/practice` (CPU
  throttling of 1 and of 8, with the scripts delayed and not), the prerendered page was still there at the load event.
  The case wrote a kept game with an unknown network, then reloaded. When the reload's answer was slow, the first
  load's code read the game and dropped it, and the reloaded page had no game for its notice. A player cannot meet
  this: only the test writes the storage between the load and the start.
- **Measured** at 8 times CPU throttling (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`), 20 runs of each with `--repeat-each`.
  "Held" is the reload's document held 1.5 s by `page.route`.
  - The case as it was: 20 of 20 passed not held, and 20 of 20 failed held (no notice within 5 s, the failure of the
    suite).
  - With a wait for the settings card before the write: 20 of 20 passed, held and not held.
- **The change:** `keepBefore` writes the storage with `page.addInitScript` before the case's only load, so no reload
  remains. Hedge School's `practice-komi.spec.ts` had the same race in `keepGame`: the first load saved the finished
  game and dropped it before the reload. Its cases go on to `/review` and `/openings`, where an init script would
  write the game again, so `keepGame` waits for the settings card before its write and reload. Measured again at 8
  times throttling: Cyanotype's case held 1.5 s failed 3 of 3 as it was and passed 3 of 3 changed. Hedge School's
  `keepGame` held 60 s failed as it was (the first load sent the finished game 3.0 s after the case started) and
  passed changed.
- **The empty page** (`:359`, "the standard start in the address brings nothing, and a kept start that the engine
  cannot read stops the game"): "Play as Red" did not show within 120 s, and the screenshot showed the header over an
  empty page. It did not occur again: at 8 times throttling, 50 of 50 loads showed the card, also with each `/_app/`
  request delayed up to 2 s at random. One `/_app/` request that fails (`start.js`, the payload or a chunk) leaves
  `/practice` with only the header and no message, as in that screenshot. abscls-lwhe adds a notice for a page whose
  scripts do not load.
- **The evidence of the next failure:** `tests/page-log.ts` attaches each page error, console error, failed request,
  HTTP error and crash to a case that fails. Playwright's trace (`retain-on-failure`) is the published method for
  this evidence, but it keeps the body of each response, and these cases load the engine's files of many megabytes.
  The listeners add no time that the suite shows: the three spec files that use it took 227.9 s, 2.2 s and 25.6 s.

### Cyanotype removes earlier engine results, as Hedge School (2026-11-11)

Beads abscls-8tl1.30. Design 20 ("Consequences" and "Where it is"), design 29 and design 33 ("The engine's files",
item 1, "The player's games", item 12, and "The gaps from Hedge School") changed, and Cyanotype's `engine.lock.json`.
Cyanotype kept every result of every engine: its first release has none of an earlier one, but its next release with
a new search or a new file of the network would add a set.

- **One removal for both sites:** the rule (`unneededResults`) and the transaction (`removeUnneeded`) moved out of
  Hedge School's `src/lib/game/earlierResults.ts` into `packages/analysis/src/earlierResults.ts`. The start at the
  site's start (`removeUnreadResults`) and the build's engine files (`engineFiles`) went into `cache.ts`. Each site's
  `earlierResults.ts` gives its engine (its `engine.lock.json`) and its reader of games (`readGames`), and each site's
  `vite.config.ts` its engine files. Hedge School's behaviour did not change: its `earlierResults.test.ts` passes
  with no change.
- **A game's id is its key:** the removal reads the games as the list does: the store's reader of games
  (`games.ts`, `readGames`) takes the store's entries, and gives a game with no id the id of its key. A game that
  Cyanotype's review kept before the list of games has no id of its own, and its variations are under its key.
- **An earlier result** is one that the site's engine cannot read, not one of an older release: its search is not
  the site's, or its network's file is not one that the lock ships. `unneededResults` counts the site's search with
  each shipped file as the site's own. Hedge School's lock keeps the earlier networks too (design 09), so a release
  that adds a network removes nothing. Cyanotype's lock ships one network. The issue that keeps the earlier ones in
  it (abscls-8tl1.54) is deferred. Until that issue lands, a Blueprints release whose lock replaces Stamp Duty 0.2
  makes the next start remove every result of Stamp Duty 0.2: no review snapshot opens without its network. Checked

  `engine-91ab0b7d`, and nor does a later release with the same search and file, or one that adds a network beside
  it. A release whose lock drops the file, or with a new search, removes all of them when no game reads them. With a
  game reviewed by them, it keeps what the game's review snapshot shows: each position of its line at the review's

- **The store in memory of the unit tests** (`packages/storage/src/memoryDb.ts`) now answers the reads of a store's

  test could run a removal.

  2 threads in the machine's queue (`apps/hedgeschool/tests/cyanotype-earlier-results.spec.ts`: three runs, and two
  in the whole suite). The store held 5,184 results and two games: the stored review's 81 results (13.8 kB each on
  average as JSON) and 63 copies of them under other keys. The start removed 5,063 and kept 121: the site's own 81,

- **The lock lists `engine-91ab0b7d`'s CPU module:** Cyanotype's lock gave its CPU module no `sameSearchAs`, so it
  did not list the CPU module of `engine-91ab0b7d` (`28775af7…`), whose search is the same (design 20, item 7, and
  design 33, "The engine's files"). A test took the real mark of a game that `engine-91ab0b7d` reviewed: the stored
  review's mark before the fixture took `engine-887be290`'s review. With that lock, the site counted the game as
  reviewed by an earlier engine (`reviewAgainWhy` gave "engine"). Its review snapshot left out the site's own search,
  so none opened. The site then reviewed the game again, with the notice that the engine changed. A review file of

- **With an analysis file's own network** ("An analysis file opens with its own network", abscls-mgme): the removal
  takes none of the results that the board reads. An analysis file keeps only results of the site's search and of a

### One rule for a draw in the value at the game's end and in Cyanotype's kept result (2026-11-11)

### Practice's page parts in packages/practice (2026-11-11)

Beads abscls-8tl1.15. Design 24 (item 9 and "Where it is"), design 29 ("Where it is") and design 33 ("What it shares
with Hedge School") changed. Cyanotype's Practice copied parts of Hedge School's page and game. They move into
`@abstractclass/practice`, as design 29, item 11, asks. No file moved, so the work has no commit of renames.

- **The game's flow:** `packages/practice/src/game.svelte.ts` (`PracticeGame`) holds the turns, the bot's timed turn,
  the takeback and its reach, Resign, Abort and the stop on an error. It also holds the bot's set-up (its build and
  the game's settings), its move, and the refusal of a move once the game has ended. Each site's game extends it with
  its own parts: its start, its positions and moves, the rules of the player's move, a check of the bot's move
  (Cyanotype checks it against the legal moves), and its end (Hedge School's save into Your games, Cyanotype's result
  by `endResult`, which did not change). The class has no switch on the game. Its tests run the flow on a game of
  words with a fake bot.
- **The page's flow:** `page.svelte.ts` (`PracticePage`) holds what both pages did the same way: the card or the game,
  the engine's start, a new game, the steps and their keys, the bot's thinking time, the question on a start brought,
  the player's notes, and the game's events. A site gives its game, its storage, its engine settings, its analytics,
  and its own parts of a game's start and end. `PracticeActions.svelte` (Take back, Abort and Resign) and
  `ConfirmEnd.svelte` (the question before Abort or Resign, with each site's words) hold that part of the markup that
  both pages repeated. `turnsOf` in `practice.ts` groups the move list's turns. Some markup is still in both pages:
  the move list's frame and its skeleton, the players' skeleton, the frame of the error and of the wait.
- **The resume rule is Hedge School's:** the page resumes a kept game only when it found one as it mounted. Before,

  this tab's engine loaded replaced the settings card that the player saw (found by abscls-z0jz's review). A start

### The pre-commit hook refuses a script without its exec bit (2026-11-11)

abscls-rcvo, the owner's decision of 2026-11-11 by the MacBook's coordinator (abscls-us46.78's third part). Git for
Windows stages a new file at mode 100644, and `core.filemode=false` keeps that mode, so a script made on Windows
reached the Mac without its exec bit. Planning's and engines' `.githooks/pre-commit` refuse such a file (planning's
hook as of c2cdbc1, engines 769a2f1b); this repository's hook now does the same.

- **The check:** the block of planning's hook, line for line but the temporary file's name. It reads the staged
  adds, modifications and type changes at index mode 100644, and refuses each one whose staged content starts with
  `#!`, with the fix in the message (`git update-index --chmod=+x -- <file>`). It runs first, in sh, with no node.
  The width check follows as before, and still only where node is found. When both fail, the hook prints both.
- **The modes:** `scripts/commit-msg.test.sh` and `scripts/pre-push.test.sh` went from 100644 to 100755. Every
  tracked file that starts with `#!` is now 100755 (the three hooks and their three tests), and every 100755 file
  starts with `#!`.
- **Limits, shared with planning's and engines' copies:** a path that starts with `:` and digits is taken for a
  header and not checked; a path with an apostrophe breaks the quoted fix in the message; the printed fix fails when
  the commit runs from a subfolder; and the hook runs one `git show` per staged file (about 0.9 s each on this machine
  under load). A fix of one goes into all three repositories.
- **Checked:** `sh scripts/pre-commit.test.sh` passed 30 cases with 2 skipped on Windows (a path `0:foo` and a path
  with a newline, which Git for Windows refuses to stage), and 29 with 1 skipped in WSL with dash and Linux Git (no
  node there). check:all passed all 19 steps. The branch's commits went through the new hook. The workflow Documents
  runs the test on each push to `dev`.

### One rule and one text for a game's result (2026-11-10)

Beads abscls-3mzd. Design 29 ("The result by the scores") holds the design now.

- **The problem:** a draw on the board read "Red won by 0.0". Several places wrote a game's result, each with its own
  code. The board's line at the game's end (`packages/review/src/ReviewView.svelte`) took Red on equal scores and
  always wrote one decimal. Each game's `endingText` (Hedge School's `enclosure.ts`, Cyanotype's `blueprints.ts`) wrote
  "A draw" or "Blue won by 27.5". Hedge School's Practice wrote "Game over: a draw." or "Game over: Blue wins by
  27.5.", and Cyanotype's Practice read its words from the stored result. Practice also had two rules for a draw: the
  stored result (`scoreResult`) took equal scores, and the outcome for the analytics (`practiceOutcome`) took a margin
  under 0.05.
- **The rule for a draw:** the margin rounded to six decimals, as a record writes it (`r+377.651497`), and a draw when
  that is 0. The audit of abscls-70t7 took 0.05 as a tolerance for floating-point error only, because every real
  margin was whole or half (engines' design 08: 737 games). That is not true of Enclosure. Its areas are exact
  rationals, so a margin can be any number at any komi (design 24, "Whole points"). The game of the fixture
  `tests/fixtures/hedgefund-review.json` ends `r+377.651497`. A tolerance of 0.05 would make a win by 0.03 a draw, so
  the rule has none. The record's rounding takes away only the error of a floating-point sum, and the rule and the
  record then agree. `resultOfScores` gives the winner, or none for a draw, and the margin. `resultOfRecord` reads a
  record's result by the same rule, and gives none for a resignation (`b+R`), a forfeit (`r+F`) or no result (`*`).
  Both were in `packages/review/src/game.ts`. abscls-5lga moved them to `packages/analysis/src/result.ts` ("One rule
  for a draw in the value at the game's end …").
- **The one text:** "A draw", or the winner and the margin with no unit, "Blue won by 28.5" (`resultText`, with the
  game's own format of a margin, `fmtMargin`). A margin that one decimal writes as 0.0 takes as many decimals as it
  needs, up to six: "Red won by 0.03" (`smallMargin`). Before, it read "won by 0.0". The two games' `endingText` now
  share one `endingWords`. These places take the rule: the board's line, the review's status line at the last move,
  the Highlights, the chart's "Result:" and the engine box's "Final margin". Before, the last two read "Result: even"
  and "Final margin 0" for a win by 0.03. Both Practice pages' lines, the stored result and the analytics' outcome
  take the rule too.
- **Practice's words:** Practice takes the review's words, after each site's frame and a full stop: "Game over. Red won
  by 377.7." (before: "Game over: Red wins by 377.7."), "Game over. A draw." and Cyanotype's "The game is over. Blue
  won by 24." The issue asked for one function in every place. Practice's own "wins by" and "a draw" would need a
  second form of the words. A look compared Hedge School's Practice on dev `e3897254` and on the branch, built, in
  headless Chromium, with the fixture's whole game kept in Practice at komi 0. It showed the win. It showed no draw:
  no test game ends within 0.05 of one, and Practice and the Analysis board take only a whole or half komi.
  Cyanotype's line now has the review's thousands separator ("Red won by 1,030"). Its words come from the position's
  scores with the komi, which agree with its stored result at every komi tested.
- **Blueprints' margin with a half komi:** the record reader takes a half komi for every game, and Blueprints' engine
  takes it. Its format of a margin rounded to whole points, so 24.5 read "won by 25". It now keeps one decimal: "24",
  "24.5", "1,024". Blueprints' records keep their half komi for now.
- **Tests:** cases for a draw in `packages/review/src/game.test.ts`, and for a floating-point draw in
  `packages/practice/src/practice.test.ts` and Hedge School's `src/lib/review/enclosure.test.ts`. All three have the
  records `r+0.03` (a win), `b+0.0000004` (a draw) and `b+0.000001`. Cyanotype's new `blueprints.test.ts` has `b+24.5`
  and `r+0.5`. Cyanotype's `stampduty.engine.test.ts` checks that the Practice line and the stored result say the same
  at komis 0, 300, -300, -730 and -1000 ("Red won by 730" to "Blue won by 270", and "A draw" at -730). Hedge School's
  `src/lib/practice/practice.test.ts` had the case `practiceOutcome([50.02, 50])`: it was a draw by the old rule, and
  is a loss now.
- **Checks:** `npm run check:all` passed all 18 steps, with no node test skipped, and the layout tests 243 of 243 in
  Chromium. Merged to dev `9a3e86f7` in one train with abscls-x2d0 and abscls-fqm7: the site suite on the train passed
  244 with no skip. CI passed, and the release check passed on both dev sites.
- **Left for later** (abscls-5lga): the value at the game's end (`resultWin`) took a strict sign, and Cyanotype's
  stored result at komi 0 took the engine's own result. The importers keep the other site's winner: their records
  state that site's result, so the review proposed no change.

### A check that each step for the owner stands alone (2026-11-11)

Beads abscls-pkdr (the check, merged to dev `4b2ea528`) and abscls-opig (this entry, the writing rule, one helper for
both document checks, and the steps to roll back).

- **Why:** on 2026-11-09 the owner asked for the steps to set up Cyanotype's analytics. The section of
  `docs/hosting.md` that gave them (abscls-8tl1.48's branch, `54e1c960`) sent the reader elsewhere for what to do:
  "do the four steps of section 4's 'The owner's own visits'", "as design 17's … lists them", "as section 5, step 2,
  does" and "as Hedge School's property has them". The coordinator passed them on as they were, and the owner could
  not follow them. The retro of that day asked for a check, so that a document cannot give such a step again.
- **The check:** `scripts/owner-steps.mjs`, the step `owner-steps` of `npm run check:all` (after `package-imports`),
  and so of the Tests workflow. It reads every Markdown file under `docs/`, the decision logs too, and each app's and
  package's README. Each refusal prints the file, the line and the phrase, with "Write the URL, the clicks and the
  values in the step itself."
- **Where a block starts and ends:** a block starts at a line that holds the marker in bold (two asterisks, then "The
  owner's steps"), or at a heading that holds "owner's steps" in any case. A heading's block runs to the next heading
  of the same or a higher level. A bold line's block runs to the next heading of any level. Another reading ends a
  bold line's block at the next heading of the level of the heading above it. That block would take in hosting.md's
  "Cyanotype's analytics", where a description gives a false refusal.
- **The seven phrases:** "steps of section", "as section N", "as … does" (at most 6 words between), "as …'s … has" (at
  most 4 words on each side), "as design NN lists" (also with "'s" and a quoted section's title), "repeat the" and "the
  same as". The words of one phrase stay in one sentence, and a phrase may wrap onto the next line. Of two phrases that
  overlap, the first one gives the one refusal. The check reads a link's text, not its target, so a link for
  information stays allowed. A fenced code block does not count. The list is short and exact: a wider list refuses
  descriptions that are complete.
- **Measured:**
  - On dev `e3897254`, before more passages had the marker: 3 blocks in 86 files, and one refusal, false:
    `hosting.md:357`, "as the job `hub` does", with the command on the line itself. The step now names the
    terminal, the folder and the command, with no comparison.
  - The review marked sections 1, 4, 5 and 7 of hosting.md: 7 blocks in 86 files on dev `4b2ea528`. The markers gave
    one more false refusal: section 5, step 1, "as one PostHog project does", a description. The sentence dropped the
    comparison.
  - On `54e1c960`'s hosting.md, the check refuses each of the four real lines (503, 509, 511 and 517) once. It also
    refuses two lines whose action is on the line: 378 (dev's line 357 above) and 499, "as section 3's are". There,
    "as … does" found no true case that another phrase did not find too. It stays, because the issue listed it.
  - Misses in the review's 34 probe phrases, reported and not added: "the same settings as the first site" ("the
    same as" needs the three words together), "Repeat steps 1 to 3", "as in section 5", "as for Hedge School", "see
    above", "follow section 4", "like the hub's", "Set up the property as Hedge School's:" (the start of the real line
    508), and a quoted section's name as the action ("The launch switch", below). Only the last one was in a block on
    dev: section 9, step 3, which now names the file, the job and the lines.
  - With the new steps to roll back: 8 blocks in 86 files on dev `9d92fee1` and this change, and no refusal.
- **Not checked:** the owner's actions outside a block. A rule that refuses an action outside a block (a bold click
  path or a dashboard's URL) also refuses descriptions. The guard there is the writing rule in
  `docs/working-notes.md`, beside the width rule: a block of steps starts with its marker, and each step names its
  URL, its clicks and its values in the step itself. The steps to register the site in Google Search Console go with
  abscls-hus.
- **The decision logs stay in the check:** they hold one block, in this file's entry "The owner's visits marked as
  internal traffic": a pointer to the steps in hosting.md. It gives no refusal. A past entry keeps its words: a
  refusal there calls for a decision on the check's scope, not for a rewrite.
- **One helper for both document checks:** the check and the width check (`scripts/doc-widths.mjs`) read a Markdown
  line by the same rules: a fenced code block does not count (`prose`), and a link's target is `](…)` with no space
  (`LINK_TARGET`). Both are in `doc-widths.mjs`, and `owner-steps.mjs` imports them. They are not in a file of their
  own, because `scripts/pre-commit.test.sh` copies `doc-widths.mjs` alone into its test repository. The results did
  not change: both checks gave the same output before and after on the 93 tracked Markdown files, on `54e1c960`'s
  hosting.md and on three made-up texts (CRLF, fences of both kinds, long links). Both test files passed unchanged.
  The review compared the old and the new code on 475 texts (the Markdown of five commits and of the working tree,
  with CRLF and fences): no difference. The planning repository's `.githooks/pre-commit` has the same width rules in
  sh, for engines. A change to the rules changes it too.
- **Roll back:** hosting.md, "Deploy, check and roll back", named no URL and no project for a rollback. It now has a
  block of steps for the projects `hedgeschool`, `cyanotype` (after its launch) and `abstractclass`, from the
  dashboard to the check of the footer's version and the revert on `dev`. One release pushes many commits, so the
  steps take each commit from the list of deployments, not from `git log`. The words come from Cloudflare's
  documentation, read on 2026-11-11. The rollbacks page of Pages
  (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/rollbacks/>, updated 2026-04-21) gives **Deployments**,
  **All deployments**, the three dotted actions menu, **Rollback to this deployment**, the confirmation window, and
  which deployments can come back. Cloudflare's other Pages pages give the **Workers & Pages** page, its URL and
  "Select your Pages project". No page names the confirmation's button, or says what the list shows of a deployment
  that Wrangler uploaded.
- **The account, read on 2026-11-11** (the Pages API, GET calls only): the projects `hedgeschool`, `cyanotype` and
  `abstractclass`, each with the production branch `main` and its site's domain. `cyanotype` has no production
  deployment, because Cyanotype is not launched. Each production deployment of `hedgeschool` holds its commit and
  the commit's first line, one deployment for each release.
- **After a rollback, the check is the footer's version, not `release-check.mjs`:** the script takes a commit for the
  footer only. It compares the engine's files with the `engine.lock.json` of its own checkout, and the header with
  its own list of links. So at an older commit it can fail although the rollback worked. The restored deployment is

### A time limit on each file of the opening book (2026-11-11)

abscls-pymm, from the review of abscls-8981. The book's loader (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/book/book.ts`) had no time
limit on a fetch. The evaluation of a variation (`judgeSearches` and `askBook` in
`packages/analysis/src/analysis.svelte.ts`) waits for the book's answer before it searches the variation's positions.
So a fetch that never ended kept the move's pulsing "…" (design 07) until the page closed. Design 32, "The book file",
now gives the limit.

- **The limit:** 30 seconds for each file, the index and each part, from the request to the end of the body
  (`BOOK_TIME_LIMIT`). Past it, the loader aborts the fetch and the file counts as not loaded. A lookup in the part
  fails with a `BookLoadError`, `bookValues` gives no values, and the review searches the position. The part leaves
  the loader's cache, so a later lookup and the table's "Try again" ask for it again. An index past its limit fails as
  an index that does not load, and the table's "Try again" asks for it again. The limit wraps any reader, so it
  rejects even when a reader does not stop.
- **The longest wait:** a lookup of a position reads its part, then the part of the position after its best move
  (`bookValues` in `results.ts`), each with its own limit. So the book holds the evaluation of a variation's move for
  at most 60 seconds.
- **The browser's own behaviour:** headless Chromium 153 kept a fetch with no headers and a fetch whose body stopped
  half way pending for 11 minutes, until the measure ended. So the limit must be the loader's.
- **The measure:** headless Chromium 153 fetched the test book's files from the dev server (port 4202), as `book.ts`
  reads them (fetch, then the JSON). The dev server serves them with the preview server's own middleware (`testBook`
  in `vite.config.ts`). One part took 2 to 15 ms at full speed. With DevTools' network presets, the largest part
  (1.json, 164 kB, 45 kB with gzip) took 0.33 s on "Fast 4G", 1.4 s on "Slow 4G" and 5.3 s on "3G". The index and the
  four parts at once took 0.6 s, 2.9 s and 11.3 s. The dev server sends the files uncompressed. 30 seconds is about
  2.7 times the whole test book on "3G", with room for the engine's larger book. No measure ran on a deployed site,
  because no deployed site serves a book.
- **Cyanotype** has no opening book. The loader is Hedge School's. The wait for the book's answer is in the shared
  analysis package. When Cyanotype's book comes, the loader and its limit move into a package (design 29).
- **Checked:** `book.test.ts` serves the cases over HTTP to the loader's own fetch. A part with no headers, a part
  whose body stops half way, and a server error each reject the lookup with a `BookLoadError`. The server sees the
  request close, and a later lookup asks again and loads the part. With mock timers, the limit holds a reader that
  never answers, the index too. A part fails again when its second request does not answer. A failure and a load
  1 ms before the limit each stop the part's timer. `reviewBook.test.ts` gives `giveBook` an `OpeningBook` whose
  variation part does not answer. The lookup waits until the limit and then gives no values, and the table's next
  lookup loads the part. `analysis.test.ts` gives `GameAnalysis` a lookup that answers no values after a while.
  "Evaluate quality" searches nothing while it waits, then searches both positions, and the move gets its quality
  label.

### release-check reads the lock of the commit that it checks (2026-11-12)

- **The change:** `release-check.mjs <base URL> <commit>` checks the deployed engine's files against the
  `engine.lock.json` of that commit (`git show`, in `packages/site/src/releaseLock.ts`). Before, it took the commit
  for the footer only and read its own checkout's lock, so after a rollback past an engine change it said FAIL
  although the rollback worked. Without a commit, it reads the checkout's lock, as before. The INFO line names the
  lock that it read. hosting.md's "Roll back", step 5, runs the script again, with each site's command written out.
- **A commit that the clone does not have** (a shallow clone, or a commit not fetched yet) stops the check before any
  request, with exit code 2 and a line that says to run `git fetch` (`git fetch --unshallow` in a shallow clone). A
  commit that has no lock at the site's path, such as one from before the site moved into `apps/hedgeschool`, stops
  it with exit code 2 too, and the line names the path.
- **Step 5 starts with `git pull` and `npm ci` in a checkout of `dev`.** `git fetch` changes no file of the checkout.
  So a checkout from before this change runs the older script, which reads the checkout's lock and says FAIL after
  the rollback, as before. The first line of the check must name the commit's lock, which the older script does not
  print. The header's links, the pages that lead home and a site's own checks still come from the checkout's script.
  A rollback past a change to them can say FAIL on their line, so step 5 tells the owner to look at them in a
  browser then.
- **Checked on 2026-11-12, read-only, from a checkout of dev at `4ad8ee9`:** on `dev.hedgeschool.pages.dev`, with no

### release-check with no commit reads the deployed commit's lock (2026-11-12)

abscls-h6md, later steps of abscls-kn89 ("release-check reads the lock of the commit that it checks").

- **The change:** with no commit, `release-check.mjs` reads the home page's footer and checks the engine's files
  against the `engine.lock.json` of the commit that the footer names, the deployed commit. Before, it read the
  checkout's lock. No workflow runs the check, and the documented runs give no commit: Cyanotype's launch checks,
  working-notes.md's "After a deploy, check the site" and the README. Each said FAIL when the checkout's lock differed
  from the deployed commit's. A commit on the command line still wins. The footer's line still checks the branch's
  commit (`origin/main`, `origin/dev`), so a run with no commit after a rollback fails on that line, and checks the
  engine's files against the deployed commit's lock. The script never reads the checkout's lock now
  (`packages/site/src/releaseLock.ts`: `commitOf`, `lockAt` and `footerCommit`).
- **The first line** names the lock's commit and where it came from: `(given: <commit>)`, or `, read from the footer`
  at its end. With a commit, it still ends with `the engine lock of commit` and the commit's 7 characters, as
  hosting.md's "Roll back", step 5, reads it.
- **The stops with exit code 2.** A home page that does not answer stops the check, with or without a commit. Before,
  Node's stack trace ended it with exit code 1. A footer that names no commit, or a footer's commit that the clone
  does not have, stops it after the home page, before the engine's checks. The line for a footer's commit names the
  footer, because the command did not name that commit. A given commit still stops it before any request. A preview
  address with no commit stops before any request too, as before: only the live site and the addresses of a site's
  `branchOf` have a branch. Its line now gives the command with `<commit>`.
- **The header's links, the pages that lead home and a site's own checks stay the checkout's,** and each of their
  lines says `(from this checkout)` after the name of its check. To take them from the commit, the check would have
  to run the commit's script, or read a data file that only commits after the change would have. Each site's script
  gives them as code, and its form changed with the moves into `apps/` and into the site package. A rollback goes to
  an older commit, so a new data file would not help the first rollbacks after it. When a marked line says FAIL,
  step 5 tells the owner to look at the header and the pages in a browser, and, for Hedge School's Function, to list
  the commits of the release that changed `functions`.

### release-check: a failed request is a FAIL line, and the checkout's marker shows only where it differs (2026-11-12)

abscls-5ouq, later steps of abscls-h6md ("release-check with no commit reads the deployed commit's lock").

- **A failed request after the home page** gives FAIL on its check's line, with `the request failed` and the reason
  (`the request failed (other side closed)`), and the check goes on to its last line and its count. Before, a
  connection that dropped in the middle of a run, or no answer from `dns.google` for the DNSSEC line, ended the check
  with Node's stack trace and exit code 1. Each check that sends a request runs it in one wrapper, `checkRequest`, the
  downloads of the engine's files too. The wrapper tells a request that got no answer from another error by the
  error's cause: Node's fetch gives a cause for a connection that fails and for a body that breaks off. Another error,
  such as a body that is not JSON or a wrong SHA-256, gives FAIL with its message, as the downloads' lines did before.
  So a manifest whose body breaks off fails its own line, and a manifest that is not JSON still names no file. A home
  page that does not answer still stops the check with exit code 2, and so does a home page whose body breaks off. A
  site's own checks take the same form, `check(name, run)`: `run()` sends the requests and gives the result, so a
  failed request names its check.
- **The marker `(from this checkout)`** now shows only when the code that gives the marked lines differs between the
  checked commit and the checkout's working tree. `checkoutDiffers`, in `packages/site/src/releaseLock.ts`, compares
  them with `git diff --quiet <commit> -- <files>`. The checked commit is the commit whose lock the check reads: the
  given commit, else the footer's. The files are the site's `scripts/release-check.mjs` and
  `packages/site/src/release-check.mjs`. These two files hold the marked lines' names, expected values, requests and
  pass rules. Their other imports give none of the marked lines: `releaseLock.ts` gives the commits and the lock, and
  the engine's `artifacts.ts` the downloads. A test in `releaseLock.test.ts` keeps it so: each site's check script
  imports only the shared check. The check does not compare the whole of `packages/site`. Its components change with
  most releases, and such a change does not change what the check expects. A change anywhere in the two files marks
  the lines, a change to a comment too, because the check compares files, not the code of each line. A commit from
  before the move into `apps/` and `packages/site` does not have the two files, so its lines have the marker. When Git
  cannot compare the files, the check marks the lines too, because a mark too many misleads less than one too few.
  `git diff` finds no difference in a file that Git does not track, such as a new script or a path in another letter
  case on Windows, so `git ls-files --error-unmatch` checks the paths first. So a run on a deployment of the
  checkout's own commit shows no marker. After a rollback, a marked FAIL can come from a change to the check since
  that release, and a FAIL with no marker shows a fault of the site. hosting.md's "Roll back", step 5, sends the owner
  to the browser for a marked FAIL on the header or on a page that leads home. For a marked FAIL on the Function, it
  sends the owner to `git log <the commit of the release before>..HEAD -- scripts/release-check.mjs`. The range ends
  at `HEAD` because step 5 runs the check in a checkout of `dev`, which can hold changes after the deployment undone.
- **Checked on 2026-11-12, read-only, from a checkout of the change on dev `0e119d5`:** `dev.hedgeschool.pages.dev`
  with no commit, PASS, 15 of 15. The live site with no commit (`8621232`), PASS, 16 of 16.
  `dev.cyanotype-ztp.pages.dev` with no commit, PASS, 11 of 11. `dev.hedgeschool.pages.dev` with `06ff7684` (before
  abscls-h6md changed the shared script), FAIL, 14 of 15: the footer alone. Each of these runs marked its lines, as it
  should: the change itself makes the checkout's two files differ from each deployed commit. A local server whose
  footer named the commit of the change gave no marker on either site. A local server that answered the home page and
  dropped every other connection, with a `dns.google` that did not answer, gave FAIL with `the request failed` and the
  reason on each line that sends a request, and `not in the manifest` on the lines that need the manifest. Its last
  line was `release-check: FAIL ..., 4 of 16 checks` (Cyanotype's, 4 of 12), exit code 1. A manifest whose body broke
  off gave FAIL with `the request failed (other side closed)` on its line. A home page whose body broke off, and a
  port that refused the connection, each with and without a commit, stopped with exit code 2.

### Why a move is bad: the three futures' prototype stops (2026-11-12)

abscls-ntkp. The owner's verdict on 2026-11-12: stop. The prototype (the page `/lab/three-futures` and the script
`scripts/measure/three-futures.mjs`, commit `cfbcb0a6`) stays on the local branch `prototype/abscls-ntkp`, not on dev.

- **The idea:** at a Mistake or a Blunder, compare the mover's score lead after three choices: the engine's best turn,
  the turn played, and a pass (the search of Show threat). The pattern of the three was to name the reason: a threat
  that the player ignored, a turn worse than a pass, or a smaller move.
- **What the prototype measured:** 20 cases (9 Mistakes, 11 Blunders) in 4 games: the test fixture's game and three
  games of the practice bot against itself at 1 visit a side. Each search used the Lite review's setting (HedgeFund
  0.2 Lite, 512 visits).
  - A pass costs a whole turn: the best turn less the pass, median 405.6 points (25.8 to 526.5). In Enclosure a pass
    measures what a turn is worth, not a threat.
  - The turn played kept most of that: median 0.80 of it (0.37 to 0.91). So no pattern of the issue fired: 20 of 20
    cases gave only the three numbers.
  - A rule by where the two turns stand against the threat's line gave 4 "Ignored a threat", 2 "A smaller move" and
    14 cases with only the numbers. It needed a second round on the owner's games to test it.
  - The cost: 2 more searches a case, a mean of 10.3 s each at 512 visits on one CPU thread.
- **Why stop:** a comparison with a pass does not give a reason that a player can use. site-coord recommended stop.
  The full report is in the issue's comments.

### Cyanotype's header links show from 740 pixels (2026-11-12)

abscls-8tl1.89. At 640 and 650 pixels, Cyanotype's theme menu went past the header's content box, and at 640 pixels
past the window, which cut the ◐. The layout sweep did not see it: nothing clips the button, and the page does not
scroll sideways.

  Cyanotype's two navs show (its root layout). Both come at the same width, and the row did not fit them.

  right edge of each child of the header against the header's content box. In Segoe UI (Windows), 640 and 650 pixels
  failed: the button ran from 615.5 to 643.5 pixels, 19.5 pixels past the content edge at 640. The row first fitted at
  660, with no room to spare. In DejaVu Sans (Linux's, as in CI's runs: the fonts of WSL's Ubuntu, loaded as web fonts
  over the page's own), every width from 640 to 720 failed. At 640 the button ended at 708.7, 84.7 pixels past the
  edge, and the second nav went past it too. The row first fitted at 730 pixels, with 5 pixels to spare. Hedge School's
  header fitted at every width in both fonts.
- **The change:** Cyanotype's navs show from 740 pixels (`min-[740px]`, `max-[740px]` in its root layout), in place of
  640. Below 740, the site's menu holds the links, as below 640 before. The menu shows Tools from 640, as before, so
  the footer's Tools link stays a phone's alone. The header is as before at 740 pixels and wider, and on Hedge School
  at every width.
- **The room at 740 pixels,** measured in the review as the content box less the children's widths and the gaps
  between them, at a height of 700: about 50 pixels in Segoe UI. In DejaVu Sans the children stay inside the box, but
  only because the name narrows. From 740 to 760 pixels, "Early Access" goes onto a second line and the header grows
  by one pixel, to 49 (at 740 the name gives up 23 pixels, from 248 to 225). From 770 the row fits on one line of
  text, with 7 pixels to spare.
- **Why not a smaller gap:** the header's gap is SiteFrame's, so it would change Hedge School's header too, at widths
  where it fits. The navs' own gaps (18 pixels, four of them) and the header's (24 pixels, three of them) give at most
  60 pixels back at 640, and DejaVu Sans needs 85. A width of 730 fits with 5 pixels to spare, too few for one more
  link, so the change takes 740.
- **The test:** a rule of the sweep, beside "the header is one row" (`problems()` in the layout test): each child of
  the header that shows stays inside the header's content box, within half a pixel. So every page's sweep checks it,
  on both sites, at every width and height. The rule looks at the header's own children only. The general rule "a
  child of a one-line flex row stays inside its row" stays out (abscls-0nax found it too wide for every page). On
  dev's build, the sweep of Cyanotype's home page failed with it at 640 and 650 pixels at each of the three heights:
  the theme menu's button ran from 615.5 to 643.5 in a content box from 16 to 624. In DejaVu Sans, the same rule

  Cyanotype's menu below 740 pixels.

### release-check and the engine step give one reason for a failed request (2026-11-12)

- **One reason for a failed request:** `fetchReason` in `packages/engine/src/errors.ts` gives it to both scripts that
  fetch in Node, the engine step (`fetch-engine.mjs`) and the shared release-check
  (`packages/site/src/release-check.mjs`). Before, each script had its own copy, in opposite orders. The shared one
  takes the cause's message first, then the cause's code, then the error's own message, as release-check did. The
  message says more than the code: Node's fetch to a host that does not exist gives `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND
  no-such-host.invalid` as its cause's message and `ENOTFOUND` as its code. The code comes next, for a cause with an
  empty message: Node's fetch to `localhost` on a port with no server gives an `AggregateError` with an empty message
  and the code `ECONNREFUSED` (both on Node 26, on this machine). So the engine step's error now names the cause's
  message where it named the code. release-check's lines do not change. The site package imports `errors.ts` from the
  engine package as it imports `artifacts.ts`, so release-check still has the engine package as its one dependency
  outside the site package. `errors.ts` decides no line's PASS or FAIL. It gives only the reason in a FAIL's line or
  in a stop's line, so the marker `(from this checkout)` does not need to compare it.
- **Design 29** now says that `releaseLock.ts` also gives `checkoutDiffers`, and that release-check takes the reason
  from the engine package.
- **The marker stays coarse:** a change anywhere in the two compared files marks the lines, a comment too. This
  change to `packages/site/src/release-check.mjs` marks every checkout line for each commit before it.

### The last move's tooltip says "Result:" when the rules ended the game (2026-11-12)

abscls-vg8i, a later step of abscls-iynz. Designs 06 and 29 changed.

- **Why:** GLOSSARY.md's "Lead" is the engine's estimate. After a game's last move, when the rules ended the game,
  the move's tooltip in the move list gives the game's result there (since abscls-iynz), not an estimate. The chart's
  note on the same position wrote it as "Result: Red +0.03", and the tooltip as "Lead: Red +0.03": one number had two
  names on one page. Both now say "Result:".
- **One rule:** `leadOrResult` in `packages/review/src/ReviewView.svelte` gives the word and the number together, to
  the move's tooltip and to the chart's note. The condition (the last position, and the rules ended the game) is in it
  only. The chart adds " · first estimate" only where a search is shallow, and the game's end is always settled.
- **What players see,** on both sites (the review is shared), by move (Hedge School's "Edge"), and by turn on the last
  move's button (the move buttons come from one snippet): a win by 0.03 read "Lead: Red +0.03" and now reads "Result:
  Red +0.03". A win by 0.5 or more ("Lead: Red +27.5") and a draw ("Lead: even") read "Result: Red +27.5" and "Result:
  even", as the chart's note already did. Every other move keeps "Lead:". A record that ends before the rules end the
  game keeps "Lead:" on its last move, because there the number is the engine's estimate. By turn, the turn's own
  tooltip has no lead, so nothing changes there.
- **The test:** `apps/hedgeschool/tests/last-move-result.spec.ts`, by move and by turn, with the engine off. On Hedge
  School it opens `tests/fixtures/hedgefund-review.json` (the rules end it at `r+377.651497`) and
  `tests/fixtures/twin-turn-review.json` (the record ends after turn 7). On Cyanotype it opens the whole test game
  with the results of `tests/fixtures/cyanotype-whole-review.json` (the rules end it at `r+730`) and the game up to
  turn 20. It fails when the last move's tooltip does not hold the chart's note at the end, when that note does not
  say "Result:" for a game that the rules ended or "Lead:" for a record that ends early, and when any other tooltip
  says "Result:".
- **Each check fails for its own fault,** in each of the 8 cases (both sites, by move and by turn, both endings),
  on builds of both sites from a changed `ReviewView.svelte`:
  - `leadOrResult` gives "Result:" on the wrong last move (the record that ends early, not the game that the rules
    ended): the chart's note at the end has the wrong word ("Lead: Red +377.7", "Result: Red +2.2").
  - The last move's tooltip alone takes the other word: the tooltip does not hold the chart's note ("Lead: Red
    +377.7" in the tooltip, "Result: Red +377.7" in the note).
  - The tooltip of the move before the last says "Result:": the check of the other moves names it ("move 119:
    Excellent: 0.0% · +1.4 · Result: Red +377.4").

### Hedge School's partner code in packages/ (2026-11-13)

Beads abscls-8tl1.74. Design 18 ("Where it is") and design 29 (item 11, "Where it is") changed. Design 33 ("Partner
sites") asks for the partner parts in the packages before Cyanotype uses them. The parts that are not Enclosure's
move, with each site's parts as parameters. Hedge School's behaviour stays the same: its messages (`hedge-school:*`,
protocol 1), its list, its texts and its events.

- **The partners' code** is in `packages/import/src/partners.ts`. `partnerSite` takes the site's parts: the start of
  its messages' names (`hedge-school`), its name in the texts (`Hedge School`), its list of partners and its test
  switch. It gives `partnerOf`, `gamePartner`, `saveToPartner` and `receiveKeptReview`, as `gameStore` gives a site's
  store. `receiveFromPartner` stays inside: only `receiveKeptReview` calls it. The test site ("the local test
  site", `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`) is in the package. Each site reads its own `VITE_PARTNER_TEST`. Hedge School's
  `src/lib/game/partners.ts` keeps `PARTNERS` (enclosuregame.com) and gives its parts.

  The receiving step refuses a site that is not a partner with "the link names a site that is not one of Hedge
  School's partners". The site's name keeps that text.
- **A kept review's receiving step** (`receiveKeptReview`) finds the partner by its page's origin. It tells the page
  the partner's name (`waiting`) and receives the file. It loads the file with the site's loader (`load`), and keeps
  the save page (`keep`, the shared store's `setGamePartner`). Hedge School's `Arrival.svelte` keeps its phases, its
  texts, its events and the review's opening. The import package depends on no other package, so the store's call is
  a step that the site gives.
- **The stored game's partner** (`partner`, `setGamePartner`) is in `packages/analysis/src/games.ts`. Its type there,
  `KeptPartner`, has the shape of the import package's `GamePartner`: the analysis package does not depend on the
  import package, and the move adds no dependency between the packages. `gameStore` no longer takes a site's own
  type of stored game: Hedge School's partner was the only field that a site kept beyond the shared ones.
- **"Save to …"** (`reviewExports`) is in `packages/review/src/exports.ts`. Hedge School's `reviewFile.ts` gives it on,
  and keeps `deliverExport`'s partner case, which calls the shared `saveToPartner`. Cyanotype's menu stays as it is
  until abscls-8tl1.75.
- **The tests:** `packages/import/src/partners.test.ts` checks the shared code with a made-up partner and a site's
  own messages: the save page's checks, the test switch, and both exchanges of messages with a page's window made in
  the test. Hedge School's `partners.test.ts`, which checks its list, is unchanged.
- **The bodies, compared** line by line with the code before the move. The site's parts replace Hedge School's
  constants: the messages' names, `PARTNERS`, the test site's switch, the site's name and the arrival's steps. The
  messages' type now reads any name. One local name in `receiveFromPartner` changed: the review received is `sent`,
  because `review` names the message. Nothing else changed.

### The end of a record that ends early is a first estimate until its search is deep (2026-11-13)

abscls-fcvt. Design 06 changed.

- **Why:** the advantage chart counted the last position as settled for every record. A record that ends before the
  rules end the game has a search at its end, as any position: the sweep and the label stage search it
  (`analysis.svelte.ts`, `passCount`). So while the end had only the sweep's result (32 visits), the chart drew the
  end as settled. Its note at the end had no " · first estimate". The review's model already had the right rule: its
  end is the result only when the rules ended the game.
- **One rule:** the review's model (`packages/analysis/src/model.ts`, `review`) gives `endedByRules` on the review,
  from its own rule for the end. The view reads it in `chartSettled`, `leadOrResult`, the status line and the summary
  (`packages/review/src/ReviewView.svelte`). The annotated record reads it too (`packages/analysis/src/annotate.ts`).
  Neither works the rule out again from the last position. The two rules differed only for a record with no last
  position, which the model counts as ended. No page makes one: the review's data (`analysis.svelte.ts`, `data`) has
  one position more than its moves. Each game's `ending` still reads the last position for the outcome's words
  (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/review/enclosure.ts`, `apps/cyanotype/src/lib/review/blueprints.ts`). Cyanotype's counts
  a record with no last position as not ended.
- **What players see,** on both sites (the review is shared), by move and by turn. At the end of a record that ends
  early, until the label stage has searched the end, the chart draws the end faint. The legend shows "Win chance,
  first estimate". The note says "Lead: Red +21.9 · first estimate" in place of "Lead: Red +21.9" on Hedge School's
  test record, and "Lead: Red +106.7 · first estimate" on Cyanotype's. Once the end's search has the review's depth,
  nothing changes. A game that the rules ended keeps "Result:" with no " · first estimate" ("Result: Red +377.7",
  "Result: Red +730.0"), before and after.
- **The test:** `apps/hedgeschool/tests/last-move-result.spec.ts`, by move and by turn, with the engine off. On Hedge
  School it opens `tests/fixtures/twin-turn-review.json` with its end's result at the sweep's visits. On Cyanotype it
  opens the test game up to turn 20 with the stored results, less the end's result at the review's depth. Each of the
  4 cases checks the note and the legend. Each failed on builds of both sites from dev's code: the note had no
  " · first estimate". Each passes after the change, with the spec's other 8 cases. In those 8 cases every result has
  the review's depth, and they check that the legend shows no first estimate.
- **Each case catches its own fault:** six breaks of the view's rule, each in a build of Hedge School, failed only
  the cases meant to catch them, by edge and by turn. The old rule (`i === last || deepEnough`) failed the early-end
  cases at the note. A legend that skips the last position failed them at the legend. `deepEnough` alone failed the
  "Result:" cases at the note, and a legend by depth alone failed them at the legend. An end that only `endedByRules`
  settles failed the "Lead:" cases of a deep early end at the tooltip. A legend that is on at every early end failed
  them at the legend. The model's `endedByRules` always true, or always false, fails the unit test
  (`packages/analysis/src/game.test.ts`).

### Cyanotype keeps its practice games, as Hedge School's (2026-11-13)

abscls-8tl1.50, from the decision of 2026-11-06 to build this gap of design 33, with the Analysis board's komi of
2026-11-07 in the same work. A game against Stamp Duty that ends goes into Your games for its review, and in a build
that stores games, to Cyanotype's own D1 database through a Pages Function, as Hedge School's games against HedgeFund
(design 25, design 33, "The stored games").

- **Before the change,** on a build of dev at 5183d8a: a game that ended left the browser. The page showed only "New
  game", the Review tab listed nothing, Abort said "You cannot continue it after this", and the Privacy page said
  "no server of its own".
- **Moved, not copied** (design 29): the stored game and its check, the Function's handlers, the sending and its queue,
  the record's tags and turns, the stored game's bookkeeping in the game's flow, and the Privacy page's section and
  choices, into `packages/practice`. Hedge School's files call them, with its behaviour and words unchanged: its
  `stored.test.ts` and `practice.test.ts` pass as before. Each site gives its game's part: a move's form for the

### An image of a line in the player's theme (2026-11-13)

abscls-xud1. Design 07 (item 17) and design 21 changed.

- **Asked for:** "Copy static", "Save static" and "Save animated" in the move menu, in a review and on the Analysis
  board, drew the light look in the dark theme too. The image of a line should follow the theme that the player sees.
- **Decided:** the image takes the theme that the page shows when the player chooses the item: the light look in the
  light theme, the dark look in the dark theme. With the theme "System", the image takes the theme that the page
  shows (`data-theme` on the page, `theme.svelte.ts`). The image then matches the board on the player's screen.
- **What this replaces:** "The look: light, in either theme" ("An image of a line", above). That entry kept one look
  for the contrast on paper and in chats of either background, and so that the images of one line look alike whoever
  made them. A player who uses the dark theme studies the dark board, and shares what they see. The dark board keeps
  the contrast of its edges, regions and numbers, as on the screen. A player who wants the light image for paper or for
  a light forum chooses the light theme first. Images of one line now differ by the theme of whoever made them.
- **How** (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/board/boardImage.ts`): the board that the image draws apart from the page sets no
  theme of its own, so it takes the page's tokens, and Tailwind's `dark:` variant reads the page's `data-theme`. The
  caption's background and text take the same theme's `--panel`, `--text` and `--muted`. The site reads a board's
  styles and those colours in one task, which a change of theme cannot break into. A change of theme while the page
  is open reaches the next image. The note's "Save image", after a refused copy, saves the same file that the copy
  made, so its image keeps the copy's theme.
- **The animated image** styles each frame's board just before it draws it, and checks the page's theme in the same
  task. A change of theme between two frames starts the image again, in the new theme. So no image mixes the two
  themes. The first build styled all the frames in the player's click instead. For the line of the whole game of
  `tests/fixtures/hedgefund-review.json` (120 edges, 122 frames), in headless Chromium on the CPU, the click's task
  then took 1.5 seconds (1,509 ms in the light theme, 1,443 ms in the dark theme), against 448 to 561 ms for the GIF's
  encoding. The page also kept every frame's SVG until the end: the heap grew by 207 to 228 MB. With one frame at a
  time, on the same line, in two runs, the longest task is the GIF's encoding (442 to 740 ms). A frame's task takes 50
  to 105 ms, and the heap grows by 74 to 115 MB. The whole image takes 4.8 to 8.2 seconds, by the machine's load.
- **The selector `[data-theme="light"]`:** only the page's root has a `data-theme` now (`theme.svelte.ts`). The light
  blocks of `site.css`, `review.css` and each site's `app.css` keep the opening `:root, [data-theme="light"]`, because
  `themeTokens.ts` finds each light block by it. There the selector adds nothing to `:root`. The `dark:` variant in
  `site.css` lost its `:not()` clause, which kept `dark:` off inside a light element. The comments that named the image
  of a line changed.
- **Cyanotype** makes no image of a line yet (its view has no `image`, abscls-8tl1.43), so nothing changed there.
- **The test:** `apps/hedgeschool/tests/line-image-theme.spec.ts`, in headless Chromium, with the engine off. It has
  two cases: a review of `tests/fixtures/hedgefund-review.json` (the line of the game's first 10 edges) and the
  Analysis board (a record of 3 edges). Each case runs in the light theme and then in the dark theme, on the same
  page. It decodes each image as a viewer shows it:
  - The PNG that "Copy static" copies, the PNG that "Save static" saves, and the PNG that the note's "Save image" saves
    after a refused copy. The page changes to the other theme before the player chooses "Save image".
  - Each frame of the GIF that "Save animated" saves. The page changes to the other theme when the site draws the
    first frame's board.
- **What the test checks:** in each image, the caption's background is the theme's `--panel`, and the board's is the
  theme's `--board-bg`. The three PNGs have the same pixels. All the GIF's frames have one theme, the new one. Both
  cases pass. The light images of both places are the same files, byte for byte, before and after the change.
- **Each check fails for its own fault** (soft checks, so that a run names every check that fails). The review built
  the site with one fault at a time, and both cases failed each time:
  - The light theme forced on the board: the caption and the board of each dark image.
  - The caption's colours read from the light theme only: the caption of each dark image, and no board.
  - Each frame styled with no check of the theme: only the animated image (one theme in all frames, and the new
    theme).
  - The note's "Save image" that draws a new image: only the image after a refused copy, its colours and its pixels.

### The book's time-limit case runs on its own clock (2026-11-14)

Beads abscls-heum, after abscls-wtdm ("A book part of another form fails as a part that fails, and the book's
time-limit test by file").

- **The failure:** the case "a part that does not answer in the time limit counts as not loaded"
  (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/book/book.test.ts`) failed at "no headers: one request, then one more" (1 !== 2). It
  failed in two site suites, in check:all's site-test, while other jobs held every thread of the machine. When it ran
  alone, it passed.
- **The cause:** the test server and the loader share one Node process and one event loop. The start part's read
  started a real timer of 150 ms. Sometimes the process did not run for 150 ms after the read started. The event loop
  then ran its timers before its input, so the timer aborted the fetch before the server read the request. The server
  counted only the later request. The case also took the abort as proof that the loader stopped its request, because
  the server had no request open. A copy of the old case that blocks the event loop for 200 ms after `openBook` fails
  at the same assertion in each run. No other path gives 1 !== 2: only the two reads with the short limit can end
  before the server counts them, and a request that the server counted stays counted.
- **How it differs from abscls-wtdm:** there, the index and two other reads took the short limit, so the server's hold
  of 300 ms made them fail. The limit by file fixed that. Here, the short limit of the start part itself raced the
  request, in real time.
- **Not in the loader:** a read that does not reach the server within its limit counts as not loaded, as design 32
  says ("A file that does not answer"). A player sees no change.
- **The change, in the case only:** the case mocks `setTimeout` (`t.mock.timers`). A limit and the server's hold end
  only when the case moves the clock. The case moves it only after the event that it waits for: the server has the
  request (`next` of the test server). For half a body, the loader also has the headers (the diagnostics channel
  `undici:request:headers` of Node's fetch). The check "not before the time limit" moves the clock to 1 ms before the
  limit and requires the lookup to be still pending. The server holds its answers with the global `setTimeout`,
  because a named import of `node:timers/promises` (the old case's `delay`) keeps the real timer under the mock. Node's
  fetch (undici) also starts its own timers with `setTimeout`, so they run on the case's clock too. The case moves the
  clock 2.4 s in all, and the shortest of fetch's own limits (a connection's keep-alive) is 3 s. The case takes less
  than 0.1 s, not 2.5 s.
- **Checked:**
  - Each of three faults in `book.ts` fails the new case: one short limit for every file (the index fails), a loader
    that does not abort its read (the test's timeout), and a timer at half the limit ("not before the time limit").
  - Under load: a job of `scripts/machine run` had 2 threads, and 30 busy Node processes in the job kept them busy.
    The job ran beside the machine's other jobs. In a first such job, the old case passed 19 of 20 runs, and its one
    failure was the same assertion. The new case passed 20 of 20. With 6 busy processes, the old case passed 20 of 20,
    so that load did not show the failure.
  - In a second such job, the new case passed 20 of 20 on Node 26.13 and 20 of 20 on Node 24.22, the version of CI.
    The old case passed 19 of 20.
  - Node 24.22 and Node 26.13 behave the same. `book.test.ts` passes 16 of 16. A named import of
    `node:timers/promises` keeps the real timer, and its default import gets the mock. After a case that fails, the
    next case has the real `setTimeout` again.

### The chart's note gives the score at the end of a record that ends early (2026-11-14)

abscls-nwmd, from the decision of 2026-11-13 on a question of abscls-fcvt's review. Design 06 changed.

- **Why:** the advantage chart's note (`chartTip`, `packages/review/src/ReviewView.svelte`) left out "Score:" at the
  last position of every record. Its reason, that the result repeats the score, holds only when the rules ended the
  game: there the note says "Result: …". At the end of a record that ends before the rules end the game, the note
  says "Lead: …", the engine's estimate, and the score so far was in no other line of the note.
- **The rule:** the note leaves out the score at the end of a game that the rules ended only. The chart's note and
  the move's tooltip take the model's rule for the end (`R.endedByRules`, from abscls-fcvt) through one helper,
  `isResult`. `leadOrResult`, `chartSettled` and `chartTip` read it.
- **The other places agree, unchanged:** the move's tooltip (`leadOrResult`) says "Result:" only where the rules
  ended the game. The status line says "Game over" there and "The record ends here" at an early end. The summary
  under the chart adds "on the board" to the score of a record that ends early. The status line, the summary and
  the record's export (`packages/analysis/src/annotate.ts`) read `R.endedByRules` too.
- **The words of the game's outcome** in the status line and the summary come from each game's `endingText`
  (`apps/hedgeschool/src/lib/review/enclosure.ts`, `apps/cyanotype/src/lib/review/blueprints.ts`). `endingText`
  reads the last position's `over` itself, as the model does. Its default for a missing position differs on
  Cyanotype (`false`, the model's is `true`). The rules describe a position after each move, so no position is
  missing, and `endingText` agrees with the model.
- **What players see,** on both sites (the review is shared), by move and by turn, with the score line on: the note
  at the end of a record that ends early has a line "Score: …" between the lead and the area (Hedge School) or the
  stars (Cyanotype). A game that the rules ended keeps "Result:" with no score. With the score line off, no note has
  a score, as before.
- **The look:** the decision of 2026-11-14 accepted this look. Its images show the note at the end on both sites, by
  move and by turn, before and after the change. They show a record that ends early and a game that the rules ended.
- **The test:** `apps/hedgeschool/tests/last-move-result.spec.ts`, by move and by turn, with the engine off and the
  score and area lines on. Its cases of the last move's tooltip also read the chart's whole note at the end: the
  lead or the result, one "Score:" line at the end of a record that ends early only, then the area or the stars. On
  builds of both sites from dev's code (c3f841d6), the 4 early-end cases failed (no "Score:" in the note). After the
  change, the spec's 12 cases pass.

### Cyanotype's home board plays three scenes (2026-11-14)

abscls-8tl1.55. Cyanotype's home board played one scene. It plays three now, as Hedge School's does (design 33, "Where
it is"). Each scene is the 9 turns before its game's latest move with a bad label, and that move.

- **The games:** three games of Stamp Duty against itself (`scripts/selfplay.mjs`, Blue at 4 visits a move and Red at
  64), in `apps/cyanotype/src/lib/review/fixtures`. No other player's game. The first scene's game is the review's
  test game (`stamp-duty.txt`). Seed 12's game (`stamp-duty-seed12.txt`) was there already. Seed 13's
  (`stamp-duty-seed13.txt`, 120 moves, Red wins by 491) is new: 211 seconds of play, on the CPU.
- **The stored reviews:** the first scene keeps `tests/fixtures/cyanotype-review.json` (the test game to turn 20).
  The stored review of seed 12's game to turn 23 has no scene: its only bad move is its last, and a scene needs the
  move after it. So both new games have a stored review of the whole game, `cyanotype-seed12-whole-review.json` and
  `cyanotype-seed13-review.json`, in OTHER_STORED (`apps/hedgeschool/tests/cyanotype-fixture.ts`).
  `scripts/cyanotype-review-fixture.mjs` made them as it made the first: the Review tab of Cyanotype's preview in
  Playwright's headless Chromium, Lite (512 visits a position), on the CPU (`machine run`, 2 threads). The engine is
  the first scene's: search `91ab0b7d`, network `b6c96-s47076224-d3087660`. Seed 12's review took 3,273 seconds and
  seed 13's 2,998 seconds, 245 results each. The label snapshot has a file for each.
- **The scenes:** the test game from turn 10 to move 36 (a Mistake, a loss of 15%), seed 12's from turn 16 to move 49
  (an Inaccuracy, 6%), seed 13's from turn 38 to move 92 (a Mistake, 13%). 61 frames. `replay.json` grew from 122 KB
  to 640 KB (20 KB compressed with gzip): the later boards hold more cells. It loads after the page shows. `still.json`
  did not change.
- **One review for both sites:** the stored results that a review reads, the review of the game from them, the
  scene's labelled move and the moves of the turn so far are in `packages/analysis/src/homeScene.ts` now. Both sites'
  `scripts/home-replay.mjs` use it. Hedge School's script writes the same files as before, byte for byte: the review
  files of its scenes are not on this machine, so the check ran it before and after on another review file of
  Enclosure (`apps/hedgeschool/tests/fixtures/hedgefund-review.json`). `replay.json` and `still.json` had the same
  SHA-256 before and after.
- **The first scene was stale:** the committed scene came from an earlier engine (search `3ac5c2fc`, network
  `b6c96-s40806528-d2304635`), and the stored review holds the results of the current one. The labels of 16 of its 20
  frames differed from the stored review's (commit `88211cc` had left them, the entry "Cyanotype's review files, as
  Hedge School's"). Commit `77959b97` wrote them again from the stored review. The scene stayed the same.
- **The check:** `apps/hedgeschool/tests/cyanotype-home.spec.ts`. The home page plays its scenes with no worker, no
  message to a worker and no request for the engine's files. For each scene, the Review tab loads the same game with
  the same stored review, and each label of the scene's frames is the Review tab's label of that move. Cyanotype's
  `src/lib/review/labels.snapshot.engine.test.ts` needs no engine and runs in CI. It checks that each scene's stored
  review has the search and the network of `replay.json` (`made`), and that each scene shows a bad move's label and a
  good move's. The `replay.json` of dev before this change fails it.
- **Seen:** screenshots of each scene's labelled move at 1,280 and 390 pixels, light, and the first at 1,280, dark.
  The labels draw on their moves. On the fuller boards of seeds 12 and 13, the board shows the whole field, so the
  labels' badges are small.

### Cyanotype's Practice points bar: its switch and its direction (2026-11-14)

abscls-8tl1.52, a gap of design 33. Cyanotype's Practice always showed its points bar above the board. It now has
Hedge School's two settings of the bar (design 24, item 12): the switch "Points bar" and the choice "Direction",
Horizontal above the board or Vertical beside it. They are in the display settings, in the group Score, before Sound,
with Hedge School's words.

- **Moved, not copied** (design 29, item 11): the bar, its settings and their store went from Hedge School's Practice
  page into `packages/practice`. `PointsBar.svelte` draws the bar in either direction, `ScoreSettings.svelte` holds
  the group Score, `scoreDisplay.svelte.ts` keeps the settings and sends the feature events ("practice bar",
  "practice area", "practice direction"), and `practice.ts` gives `scoreStore`, `upright` and `gaugeWidth`. Hedge
  School keeps its key `hedge-school:practice-display:2` and its values.
- **No area:** Blueprints has no area, so Cyanotype offers no switch "Area" and no area lane. The store takes an
  `area` flag: without it, a kept `area: true` loads as false.
- **The key:** `cyanotype:practice-display:1`, with Hedge School's values (`bar`, `area`, `form`). The version counts
  the key's own history, as Cyanotype's other keys do, so it is 1 where Hedge School's is 2.
- **The upright bar** is left of the board's box and as high as it. The practice frame's fill form, Cyanotype's, now
  takes the gauge as the square form does: the players' row then starts at the box's left edge. On a phone the board's
  box holds the board and the hands, so the bar runs beside both, as on Cyanotype's review.
- **Checked:** the unit tests of `scoreStore`, `upright` and `gaugeWidth`, and `svelte-check` of both apps and
  `packages/practice`. A new browser test, `practice-points-bar.spec.ts`, runs the same four cases on both sites:
  the controls and their first values, Vertical at 1,280 pixels, after a reload and at 390 pixels, the bar off after
  a reload, and a kept area, whose lane shows on Hedge School only. Hedge School had no browser case for these
  settings. Each Cyanotype case fails on the page before this change. Screenshots in headless Chromium at 1,280 and
  390 pixels show Cyanotype's bar horizontal, upright and off, its settings open, the upright bar in the dark theme,
  and Hedge School's upright bar as before.
